On October 23, 2025, DoorDash shares briefly dropped before rising 1.5%. Culper also cited a July 2025 Freedom of Information Act request suggesting DoorDash may face an undisclosed SEC investigation.

title: RXO reported 16-19% gross margins. A short seller alleged it had $7 million in cash.
points: The firm analyzed public filings and alleged that RXO shifted costs of revenue to operating expenses to report 16-19% margins while industry peers made 6-8%.
It also alleged that RXO changed its definition of EBITDA to avoid breaching debt covenants after cash fell to $7 million.
In a filing on January 23, 2026, RXO announced that Chief Accounting Officer Jason Kerr would retire on May 15, 2026.
body: RXO, Inc. is a US digital freight brokerage that spun off from XPO. The company told investors its business generated strong performance and 16-19% gross margins.

On October 22, 2025, DF Research, led by Keith Dalrymple, published a report and disclosed a position in the securities. The firm analyzed public filings and alleged that RXO shifted costs of revenue to operating expenses to report 16-19% margins while industry peers made 6-8%. It also alleged that RXO changed its definition of EBITDA to avoid breaching debt covenants after cash fell to $7 million.

In a filing on January 23, 2026, RXO announced that Chief Accounting Officer Jason Kerr would retire on May 15, 2026. By February 2026, RXO had missed fourth-quarter guidance and transitioned from unsecured credit to an asset-based loan secured by $1.23 billion in accounts receivable. DF Research called the move a forced foreclosure by lenders after RXO used $566 million of its $565 million credit line.

The $1.23 billion in receivables and the $566 million in credit used are different figures: the first is money owed to RXO, and the second is debt it drew down. On May 6, 2026, DF Research noted that RXO would report first-quarter results the next day.

title: CCC sent PLN 330 million of goods to an insolvent buyer and moved to buy it
points: NINGI said that starting in November 2024, CCC sent PLN 330 million in unwanted inventory to an insolvent franchisee called MKRI, which operates Kaes and Worldbox stores.
NINGI also alleged that CCC planned to acquire MKRI from Arca REO PSA to erase the uncollectible PLN 330 million receivable through consolidation.
These two figures are separate: PLN 330 million was the inventory and receivable figure, while PLN 267.4 million was the alleged EBITDA boost.
body: CCC SA is a Polish footwear company listed in Warsaw that presented investors with a retail turnaround.

On October 16, 2025, short seller NINGI Research published a report alleging that the turnaround was an illusion. NINGI said that starting in November 2024, CCC sent PLN 330 million in unwanted inventory to an insolvent franchisee called MKRI, which operates Kaes and Worldbox stores.
The report alleged that short-term receivables rose 112% year-over-year to PLN 535 million, with PLN 130 million past due, and that the shipments inflated group EBITDA by PLN 267.4 million.

NINGI also alleged that CCC planned to acquire MKRI from Arca REO PSA to erase the uncollectible PLN 330 million receivable through consolidation. The report said that CCC's supervisory board chairman, Wieslaw Oles, secretly controlled the seller. These two figures are separate: PLN 330 million was the inventory and receivable figure, while PLN 267.4 million was the alleged EBITDA boost.

CCC denied the allegations in a rebuttal post and video conference, saying they were false and made to profit from short positions. NINGI replied the video had confirmed several findings, including that CCC was behind on its store expansion targets.

title: Anbio Biotechnology shares fell 89.18% after a short seller report
points: A short seller earns money when a company's shares fall.
HitHawk Research also published a report involving Anbio on December 10, 2025.
Anbio Biotechnology's Class A Ordinary Shares fell 89.18% since the October 16, 2025 report.
body: Anbio Biotechnology is a Nasdaq-listed company trading under the symbol NNNN. Established in 2021 and based in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, it operates as a global supplier of in vitro diagnostics products.
On October 16, 2025, short seller HitHawk Research published a report on Anbio Biotechnology titled Engineered Exit. A short seller earns money when a company's shares fall.
HitHawk Research also published a report involving Anbio on December 10, 2025.
Anbio Biotechnology's Class A Ordinary Shares fell 89.18% since the October 16, 2025 report.

title: A $49.95 bet paid $115 on Kalshi and $107 on DraftKings
points: Short seller The Bear Cave reported that prediction market Kalshi offered better odds than DraftKings.
Spruce Point Capital Management estimated 35% to 60% downside risk for DraftKings shares.
DraftKings stock had fallen about 40% since its first article.
body: DraftKings is a Nasdaq-listed online sports betting and gaming company. Investors had viewed DraftKings and FanDuel as an effective duopoly with a high-margin base of repeat customers.

On September 18, 2025, short seller The Bear Cave reported that prediction market Kalshi offered better odds than DraftKings. The Bear Cave bet $49.95 on Kalshi to win $115 on the Buccaneers and $50 on DraftKings to win $107, and reviewed NFL Sunday game payouts showing higher returns on Kalshi.
Spruce Point Capital Management estimated 35% to 60% downside risk for DraftKings shares. DraftKings stock had fallen about 40% since its first article.

In September 2026, ProPublica reported on how DraftKings courts customers and whether its internal guardrails stop users from spiraling out of control, noting DraftKings made reporter Jake Pearson a VIP with a personal host. CEO Jason Robins told CNBC he had looked at the betting history and was proud of how the company handled it.

Regulators across the country cited ProPublica's reporting when announcing reviews of how sportsbooks incentivize users to keep betting. On November 14, 2026, ProPublica reported DraftKings had closed Pearson's account and sent him a 94-cent check.

title: A small Singapore firm bought $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips. US officials opened a probe.
points: The New York Times reported that it had visited sites in four countries, reviewed shipment records and business registrations, and interviewed more than 30 people.
The Times also reported that Megaspeed spent $4.8 billion on restricted Nvidia AI chips since June 2024 and received more than 200 shipments over 12 months.
Megaspeed chief executive James Tan denied breaking US laws, saying the company's operations were legitimate and it had cooperated with investigators.
body: Megaspeed International is a Singapore-based data center and cloud computing company. It told authorities and partners that it ran a legitimate commercial cloud business outside China.

On October 9, 2025, The New York Times reported that it had visited sites in four countries, reviewed shipment records and business registrations, and interviewed more than 30 people. Megaspeed funneled Nvidia chips to data centers in Malaysia and Indonesia that appeared to remotely serve customers in China.
The Times also reported that Megaspeed spent $4.8 billion on restricted Nvidia AI chips since June 2024 and received more than 200 shipments over 12 months.

Megaspeed chief executive James Tan denied breaking US laws, saying the company's operations were legitimate and it had cooperated with investigators. Nvidia initially stated that its own compliance checks found no evidence of chip diversion.

On November 16, 2026, the US Commerce and Justice Departments announced that their investigation into potential export control violations had started in 2024 and included an in-person check in Singapore in June 2025. Singaporean police also stated that their domestic investigation into Megaspeed remained ongoing.

title: A regulator barred Slide Insurance's CFO from serving as an officer
points: The report alleged that Slide's technology claims were significantly overstated.
Manatee Research also cited screenshots from a Florida Office of Insurance Regulation letter obtained through a public records request.
Law firm Holzer & Holzer announced an investigation into whether Slide Insurance Holdings complied with federal securities laws.
body: Slide Insurance Holdings is a $1.9 billion property and casualty insurer based in Tampa, Florida. Founded in 2021, the Nasdaq-listed company describes itself as a tech-enabled insurer and writes homeowners insurance policies.

On September 30, 2025, short seller Manatee Research published a report on Slide Insurance and disclosed a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The report alleged that Slide's technology claims were significantly overstated.

Manatee Research also cited screenshots from a Florida Office of Insurance Regulation letter obtained through a public records request. According to the report, the letter stated that Slide's President and Chief Financial Officer Jesse Schalk shall not serve as an officer or director at Slide Insurance, and warned that noncompliance could lead to suspension or revocation of the subsidiary's Certificate of Authority.
On October 7, 2025, law firm Holzer & Holzer announced an investigation into whether Slide Insurance Holdings complied with federal securities laws.

title: Richtech Robotics pitched U.S. robots. Short sellers alleged a Chinese import loop.
points: Richtech announced a Master Services Agreement with a top global retailer.
Fugazi Research published a second report and disclosed a financial interest in the securities.
Richtech shares fell 88.70% after the Fugazi report.
body: Richtech Robotics is listed on Nasdaq and tells investors it designs and makes autonomous delivery robots for restaurants and hotels. The company began as Richtech Creative Displays in 2017 and became Richtech Robotics in 2022.
In August 2025, Richtech announced a Master Services Agreement with a top global retailer. Online speculation linked the deal to Walmart and fueled a sharp rise in the share price.

On September 30, 2025, Capybara Research published a report and disclosed that its affiliates held a short position in Richtech shares, meaning it earned when the shares fell. Capybara alleged that Richtech sold rebranded Chinese robots and relied on fake partnerships, fake deals, fabricated Walmart hype, and undisclosed related-party transactions.

On October 23, 2025, Fugazi Research published a second report and disclosed a financial interest in the securities. Fugazi alleged that Richtech operated as a reseller of imported Chinese systems rather than a U.S. robotics maker. Richtech shares fell 88.70% after the Fugazi report.

title: Rezolve AI reached a $2 billion valuation with $0 in AI revenue
points: The firm interviewed former employees, checked app store listings, and tested the company's software.
Fuzzy Panda alleged that Rezolve had $0 in AI revenue the previous year and generated only about $190k in 2024 from Spanish football game tickets.
The same day, Rezolve AI rejected the report as misleading and called it a self-serving attempt to spread misinformation for profit.
body: Rezolve AI is a UK company listed on Nasdaq that sells commerce software and told investors it was an artificial intelligence company. It went public through a SPAC in late 2024 and reached a valuation of about $2 billion.

On September 29, 2025, short seller Fuzzy Panda Research published a report on the company and disclosed it held a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The firm interviewed former employees, checked app store listings, and tested the company's software.

Fuzzy Panda alleged that Rezolve had $0 in AI revenue the previous year and generated only about $190k in 2024 from Spanish football game tickets. The report also said Rezolve paid more than $147 million to Microsoft for an Azure Marketplace app that had zero reviews, and paid $93.9 million in shares to a Seychelles entity tied to chief executive Dan Wagner.
The same day, Rezolve AI rejected the report as misleading and called it a self-serving attempt to spread misinformation for profit.

title: A $500K-a-year rare-disease drug faced claims of sham trials. The stock fell 13%.
points: Scorpion Capital alleged that VYKAT XR is a $500K-a-year knockoff of a 50-year-old generic compound supported by suspect data and sham clinical trials.
Shares of Soleno fell 13% on the morning of August 15, 2025.
Law firm Hagens Berman issued a notice encouraging Soleno investors with losses from the August 15 drop to contact the firm.
body: Soleno Therapeutics, Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed company that sells VYKAT XR, a drug for hyperphagia and weight management in Prader-Willi syndrome. In October 2023, the company received FDA approval for the treatment.

On August 15, 2025, short seller Scorpion Capital published a report on the company and filed an FDA Citizen Petition. Scorpion Capital alleged that VYKAT XR is a $500K-a-year knockoff of a 50-year-old generic compound supported by suspect data and sham clinical trials.

The report also alleged that a physician's co-authored papers showed irregularities in data integrity and adherence to scientific standards, casting doubt on Soleno's trials, publications, and FDA submissions. Scorpion Capital suggested the drug could face market withdrawal or a drop in new prescriptions. Shares of Soleno fell 13% on the morning of August 15, 2025.
On September 25, 2025, law firm Hagens Berman issued a notice encouraging Soleno investors with losses from the August 15 drop to contact the firm.

title: A €5,080 Blazer in Moscow. Brunello Cucinelli Shares Fell 15%.
points: Morpheus Research published an 84-page report based partly on visits to Moscow stores.
At Moscow's TSUM store, investigators found a blazer priced at RUB 499,500, approximately €5,080, with a tag showing manufacture in Italy in March 2025.
On September 25, its shares fell as much as 15% when trading resumed after a suspension lasting nearly four hours.
body: Brunello Cucinelli is an Italian luxury fashion company known for its cashmere clothing, valued at €7 billion. The company had told investors about its Russian business, but short seller Morpheus Research alleged that its account of those operations was misleading.

On September 25, 2025, Morpheus Research published an 84-page report based partly on visits to Moscow stores. The firm held short positions in Brunello Cucinelli shares, meaning it stood to gain if the price fell.

Its secret shopper entered a Brunello Cucinelli outlet in Moscow and documented merchandise at the GUM store on Red Square. Product tags identified the manufacturer as Brunello Cucinelli SpA and the importer as its Russian subsidiary, Brunello Cucinelli RUS OOO. At Moscow's TSUM store, investigators found a blazer priced at RUB 499,500, approximately €5,080, with a tag showing manufacture in Italy in March 2025.

Morpheus alleged that the company continued operating in Russia despite EU sanctions and engaged in aggressive discounting. On September 25, its shares fell as much as 15% when trading resumed after a suspension lasting nearly four hours.
On September 30, 2025, Bloomberg described the allegations in its coverage of the report. The article identified the central accusation as misleading investors about the company's Russian operations.

title: Aya Gold & Silver reported 100 million ounces of silver. A short seller said half was phantom.
points: The firm alleged that a 2021 resource update, produced by a business associate of CEO Benoit La Salle, inflated the silver resource by over 100%, or more than 50 million ounces.
Using satellite imagery, Blue Orca claimed the mine should have yielded 6.3 million ounces by the end of the second quarter of 2025, rather than the 3.3 million ounces mined.
Aya's shares dropped as much as 22% before closing down 2.6% that day, and later rebounded.
body: Aya Gold & Silver Inc is a Canadian mining company listed in Toronto. It told investors its Zgounder mine in Morocco held a 100-million-ounce silver resource and would generate over $100 million in cash flows.

On September 25, 2025, Blue Orca Capital published a report and said it held a short position in the stock, earning when shares fall. The firm alleged that a 2021 resource update, produced by a business associate of CEO Benoit La Salle, inflated the silver resource by over 100%, or more than 50 million ounces.
Using satellite imagery, Blue Orca claimed the mine should have yielded 6.3 million ounces by the end of the second quarter of 2025, rather than the 3.3 million ounces mined.

Aya's shares dropped as much as 22% before closing down 2.6% that day, and later rebounded. The company denied the allegations, calling them inaccurate and aimed at profiting from a share drop. The share price fall and the alleged missing silver are separate figures: the first reflects market trading, while the second is an unverified claim about ore in the ground.

On December 2, 2025, Blue Orca issued an update noting that Aya's third-quarter open-pit grades fell to 123 grams per tonne and that the miner attributed lower grades to intentionally leaving high-grade ore in the ground.

title: U.S. Gold held $11.3 million in cash against a $95.5 million deficit
points: It cited the July 31, 2025 filing showing $11.3 million in cash and an accumulated deficit of roughly $95.5 million alongside $8-12M annual losses.
The cash on hand and the alleged promotional payments are different figures: the first sat in the company's accounts, while third parties paid the second.
Gold shares moved -50.13% since that report.
body: U.S. Gold Corp is a Nasdaq-listed gold exploration company that told investors in its quarterly filing it lacked funds to advance projects beyond permitting and engineering without raising new money.

On September 24, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published a report and said it held a short position, which earns when shares fall. It cited the July 31, 2025 filing showing $11.3 million in cash and an accumulated deficit of roughly $95.5 million alongside $8-12M annual losses.

BMF Reports alleged a pattern of paid promotions before share sales, citing $28,000 paid to RagingBull before a $5M offering, plus $4,000 to Stock Dads LLC and $300 to Millionaire Mindset Group in September 2025. The cash on hand and the alleged promotional payments are different figures: the first sat in the company's accounts, while third parties paid the second.
Gold shares moved -50.13% since that report.

title: goeasy reported a 9% charge-off rate. A short seller put it at 15%.
points: The firm held a short position in the stock, earning money if the shares fell.
It said the reported 9% net charge-off rate should be closer to 15%.
Goeasy denied the claims, pointing to its over $400 million loan loss provision.
body: goeasy Ltd. is a Canadian lender based in Mississauga, Ontario that provides non-prime loans and leasing through easyhome, easyfinancial, and LendCare. It told investors it had stable delinquency rates and a provision for future loan losses of over $400 million.

On September 22, 2025, Jehoshaphat Research published a report after studying the lender's accounting and comparing its 2024 annual report to the prior one. The firm held a short position in the stock, earning money if the shares fell.

Jehoshaphat Research alleged goeasy delayed about $300 million in credit losses by pushing out about $100 million through a narrower definition of charge-offs and about $200 million by burying delinquencies. It said the reported 9% net charge-off rate should be closer to 15%.

On September 24, 2025, goeasy denied the claims, pointing to its over $400 million loan loss provision. On November 6, 2025, goeasy added disclosures around its collection practices and borrower assistance, and by March 10, 2026, it had overhauled its accounting and business practices.

title: A soccer holding company pivoted to a $300 million crypto treasury
points: The report said Brera's Italian sports clubs, including Brera Milano, Juve Stabia, and UYBA Volley, generated minimal revenue and served mainly for publicity.
Fugazi Research alleged that Brera shifted toward capital-markets engineering.
The report also alleged that Executive Chairman Dan McClory held a dual role at placement agent Boustead Securities, which it said triggered formal FINRA conflict-of-interest rules.
body: Brera Holdings PLC is an Ireland-based holding company that listed on Nasdaq in January 2023. It promoted a plan to own multiple social-impact soccer clubs.

On September 22, 2025, Fugazi Research published a report on the company. The report said Brera's Italian sports clubs, including Brera Milano, Juve Stabia, and UYBA Volley, generated minimal revenue and served mainly for publicity.

Fugazi Research alleged that Brera shifted toward capital-markets engineering. It pointed to a 1-for-10 reverse stock split, warrant offerings, insider votes authorizing 10 billion new Class B shares, and a $300 million private placement payable in dollars or crypto to create a digital-asset treasury.
The report also alleged that Executive Chairman Dan McClory held a dual role at placement agent Boustead Securities, which it said triggered formal FINRA conflict-of-interest rules.

title: A major US plant nursery used J-1 cultural exchange visas to staff its Long Island site
points: The investigation said workers at the nursery faced long hours, threats of deportation and filthy accommodation.
It also found unsafe conditions that led to injuries and illness.
Kurt Weiss Greenhouses' former director said most employees had positive experiences.
body: Kurt Weiss Greenhouses is one of the largest plant nurseries in the United States, operating on Long Island. It allegedly supplies plants to Costco, Walmart and Home Depot.

In September 2025, The New York Times published an investigation into migrant workers on J-1 cultural exchange visas in the United States. Workers at Kurt Weiss Greenhouses faced exploitative working conditions.
The investigation said workers at the nursery faced long hours, threats of deportation and filthy accommodation. It also found unsafe conditions that led to injuries and illness.

The New York Times approached the companies that employed the workers, and they either denied the allegations, declined to discuss the programme or did not respond. Kurt Weiss Greenhouses' former director said most employees had positive experiences.

title: Uranium Energy reached a $5.4 billion value with no proven or probable reserves
points: The report said Uranium Energy had no proven or probable uranium reserves and traded at 42 times 2026 estimated revenue.
Spruce Point also alleged that CEO Amir Adnani had business and family ties to people convicted by the SEC, BCSC, and DOJ.
The firm estimated 65% to 85% long-term downside risk for the shares, putting their value between $1.76 and $4.33.
body: Uranium Energy Corporation is listed on NYSE American and aimed to become a leading integrated uranium explorer and producer in the United States. It grew from a former Vancouver bulletin board penny stock into a company valued at $5.4 billion.

On September 18, 2025, short-selling firm Spruce Point Capital Management published a report titled "Uranium Gold or Dirt?" after a forensic evaluation of the company. The report said Uranium Energy had no proven or probable uranium reserves and traded at 42 times 2026 estimated revenue.

Spruce Point also alleged that CEO Amir Adnani had business and family ties to people convicted by the SEC, BCSC, and DOJ. It questioned the company's audit committee, financial controls, minimal audit fees, and past safety compliance citations.

The firm estimated 65% to 85% long-term downside risk for the shares, putting their value between $1.76 and $4.33. Market capitalization is the total value of the company's shares, while estimated downside is the firm's forecast of a price drop.

title: iPro Realty was missing $10.5 million in trust funds and kept operating for months
points: In late May 2025, iPro Realty disclosed a financial shortfall after the Real Estate Council of Ontario (RECO) requested pre-inspection information.
RECO found that co-founders Rui Alves and Fedele Colucci had illegally disbursed $10.5 million from the trust accounts.
About $3 million was paid back from the sale of iPro assets, and Richer left RECO in August 2025.
body: iPro Realty was a Mississauga-based real estate brokerage that employed 2,400 agents across 17 offices in Ontario. The firm held consumer deposits and agent commissions in trust accounts.

In late May 2025, iPro Realty disclosed a financial shortfall after the Real Estate Council of Ontario (RECO) requested pre-inspection information. RECO found that co-founders Rui Alves and Fedele Colucci had illegally disbursed $10.5 million from the trust accounts.

The Toronto Star obtained residential MLS sales data and found that RECO allowed iPro Realty to participate in nearly 730 residential transactions worth more than $700 million between June 1 and August. RECO's registrar, Joseph Richer, signed an undertaking agreeing not to fine or charge the co-founders, who voluntarily terminated their registrations.

About $3 million was paid back from the sale of iPro assets, and Richer left RECO in August 2025. RECO notified Peel police's fraud bureau, launched an internal review, and a court later granted RECO's request to freeze the co-founders' assets.

title: Dexcom changed a glucose sensor component. FDA inspectors found it less accurate.
points: Hunterbrook reported that a surprise FDA inspection had uncovered an unauthorized design change to a key G7 component.
A law firm investigating the device said at least 60 people claimed hospitalization, while others alleged deaths linked to G7 problems.
Hunterbrook later described three deaths reported to the FDA following G7 problems.
body: Dexcom is a US company that sells continuous glucose monitors to help people with diabetes track their blood sugar. Its flagship G7 device was marketed as accurate enough for patients to rely on when managing their condition.

On June 26, 2026, Hunterbrook reported that a surprise FDA inspection had uncovered an unauthorized design change to a key G7 component. According to the investigation, Dexcom's internal studies found the replacement inferior by every accuracy metric, but the company sold the device anyway.

Hunterbrook interviewed more than a dozen G7 users, former employees and doctors. Former staff alleged that pressure to protect revenue margins had compromised safety. A law firm investigating the device said at least 60 people claimed hospitalization, while others alleged deaths linked to G7 problems.

Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position in Dexcom shares, which could profit if the price fell. Dexcom did not respond to repeated requests for comment about subsequent death reports. The available accounts gave no share-price movement on publication day.

Hunterbrook later described three deaths reported to the FDA following G7 problems. FDA records cited by Hunterbrook listed at least 13 deaths involving G7 devices since their 2023 launch, without establishing that the devices caused those deaths. The FDA had issued Dexcom a warning letter in March 2025.

title: Trustpilot sold review management subscriptions. Italy fined the platform $4.6 million.
points: Grizzly alleged Trustpilot created unsolicited business profiles to attract bad reviews and push firms into paying for subscriptions.
Trustpilot shares fell on December 4, 2025, and the company lost £243 million in market value in one day.
An Italian regulator fined Trustpilot $4.6 million for misleading consumers and failing to adequately verify reviews, and the shares slipped.
body: Trustpilot Group PLC is a third-party review site listed in London that sells premium memberships to businesses. The company told investors it runs a freemium model where consumers read and write reviews for free.

On December 4, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report on the company and said it was short the stock, which earns when shares fall. The firm interviewed former insiders, business owners and reputation experts.

Grizzly alleged Trustpilot created unsolicited business profiles to attract bad reviews and push firms into paying for subscriptions. It also alleged Trustpilot removed genuine negative reviews for paying clients while allowing fake reviews and scam companies to keep high ratings.
Trustpilot shares fell on December 4, 2025, and the company lost £243 million in market value in one day. The market value erased is not cash lost by the business.
On March 23, 2026, an Italian regulator fined Trustpilot $4.6 million for misleading consumers and failing to adequately verify reviews, and the shares slipped.

title: Opendoor traded at four times book value while losing money on houses
points: Martin Shkreli announced a short position against Opendoor after its shares had gained over 1,000% from their 52-week lows.
Opendoor shares fell 6.06% on Tuesday to $8.92, then rose 0.78% in after-hours trading.
The July 8 report also questioned Opendoor's plans to rely more on artificial intelligence.
body: Opendoor Technologies Inc. is a real estate company that buys and resells houses. It promoted a strategy called Opendoor 2.0, aimed at using artificial intelligence, holding houses for less time, and handling more transactions for third parties.

In September 2025, Martin Shkreli announced a short position against Opendoor after its shares had gained over 1,000% from their 52-week lows. A short seller earns when shares fall. Opendoor shares fell 6.06% on Tuesday to $8.92, then rose 0.78% in after-hours trading.

On July 8, 2026, J Capital Research published a report questioning Opendoor's business model. It said the shares traded at about four times book value even though the company made no profit and lost money when house prices stayed flat.

J Capital Research attributed those losses to sales and marketing costs, administration, stock compensation, technology, and interest expenses. It described stock compensation as unusually large relative to operating performance.

The July 8 report also questioned Opendoor's plans to rely more on artificial intelligence. J Capital Research said the company's software and computer assets were minimal, despite the technology's place in the proposed strategy.

title: CoreWeave reported a $66.8 billion backlog. Short sellers saw $9.4 billion sitting idle.
points: It estimated the company would burn $19 billion of cash in 2025 and $40 billion overall, projecting up to 90% downside for the shares.
Abelian Analysis published a second report, noting it held a short position via a September 2026 bear put spread.
Abelian Analysis also noted that Microsoft accounted for roughly 67% of CoreWeave's revenue, and that the company's fourth-quarter earnings per share missed consensus by 130%.
body: CoreWeave is a specialized cloud computing provider that rents graphics processing units for artificial intelligence workloads. Listed on Nasdaq, it told investors its revenue backlog had grown to $66.8 billion by the fourth quarter of 2025 and guided 2026 revenue to between $12 billion and $13 billion.

On September 14, 2025, short seller Kerrisdale Capital published a report arguing CoreWeave was a debt-fueled rental business generating returns below its cost of capital. It estimated the company would burn $19 billion of cash in 2025 and $40 billion overall, projecting up to 90% downside for the shares.

On February 27, 2026, Abelian Analysis published a second report, noting it held a short position via a September 2026 bear put spread. Using CoreWeave's filings, it said hardware purchased but not yet generating revenue had reached $9.4 billion, while customer payment wait times hit 182 days and each dollar of capital spending produced $0.31 of new revenue in 2025.
Abelian Analysis also noted that Microsoft accounted for roughly 67% of CoreWeave's revenue, and that the company's fourth-quarter earnings per share missed consensus by 130%.

body: Marex Group Plc is a UK broker listed on Nasdaq. It reported profits and strong operating cash flow, while short seller NINGI Research alleged its accounts overstated both.
