body: MediaAlpha, Inc. is a US insurance lead generator whose health insurance segment accounts for 47% of its trailing twelve-month revenue and most of its gross profits. The company uses websites and ads to collect personal information from consumers seeking health insurance quotes and sells those leads to partners.

On June 24, 2024, short seller Wolfpack Research published a report on MediaAlpha and disclosed it was short the stock. Wolfpack reviewed thousands of ads and hundreds of websites, spoke with dozens of partners, and created aliases that received over 400 calls.

Wolfpack answered over 50 calls and alleged that 20% of callers falsely claimed to represent a state government. The report alleged that up to 78% of MediaAlpha's health lead-buying partners ran boiler room scams or broke telemarketing laws, and that ads falsely promised free government health insurance for citizens earning less than $122k per year.

Wolfpack noted that MediaAlpha's health segment was under an ongoing Federal Trade Commission investigation that had already cost the company $5 million in legal fees, and that the FTC had previously characterized MediaAlpha websites like obamacareplans.com as deceptive. On October 1, 2025, law firm Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC announced it was investigating potential claims on behalf of MediaAlpha investors.

title: Collective Mining's Key Gold Deposit Had Drill Holes on Untitled Land, Report Said
points: Morpheus Research alleged that Collective had drilled on land without approved mining titles.
Collective had disclosed 116 applications for incomplete mining claim cells, but Morpheus said ANM had published no approvals for its outstanding applications.
Collective Mining shares fell 7% on August 6, 2025, after the report appeared.
body: Collective Mining is a Canadian company exploring mineral deposits in Colombia. Its Apollo gold discovery had helped drive a 285% share price rally since June 2022. Brokerage estimates put Apollo at 93% of the company's net asset value.

On August 6, 2025, Morpheus Research alleged that Collective had drilled on land without approved mining titles. The short seller compared Collective's drilling maps with Colombia's mining regulator ANM's title database and Google Earth Pro. Morpheus held short positions, which stood to gain if the shares fell.

The report said a significant portion of Apollo's drill holes crossed untitled land. Collective had disclosed 116 applications for incomplete mining claim cells, but Morpheus said ANM had published no approvals for its outstanding applications. The researchers also compared drilling locations with environmental maps and alleged that holes crossed protected forest buffer zones.

Collective Mining shares fell 7% on August 6, 2025, after the report appeared. On August 12, Morpheus published a response to Collective's defense, alleging that the company had misinterpreted Colombian law when justifying drilling on untitled land. Morpheus maintained its allegations.

title: United Therapeutics fought a rival drug in court for 5 years
points: The report said United Therapeutics had spent 5 years using patent lawsuits to delay Yutrepia, even as Liquidia invalidated or was found not to infringe key patents.
It also alleged that the drug pipeline was too meager to restart sales growth, citing two doctors who called a planned Tyvaso use difficult to justify.
The report concluded that United Therapeutics' legal remedies against Yutrepia appeared to be coming to an end.
body: United Therapeutics is a $13 billion commercial-stage pharmaceutical company. It sells a drug called Tyvaso and sued rival Liquidia Corp after Liquidia filed an application for a competing product named Yutrepia.

On July 29, 2025, short seller Bleecker Street Research published a report on the dispute. Funds managed by Bleecker Street held a short position in United Therapeutics and a long position in Liquidia, earning money when United Therapeutics shares fall.

The report said United Therapeutics had spent 5 years using patent lawsuits to delay Yutrepia, even as Liquidia invalidated or was found not to infringe key patents. It also alleged that the drug pipeline was too meager to restart sales growth, citing two doctors who called a planned Tyvaso use difficult to justify.
The report concluded that United Therapeutics' legal remedies against Yutrepia appeared to be coming to an end.

title: MarketWise shares fell from $60 to about $20 as it wound down Legacy Research
points: The firm analyzed web traffic data and found that Stansberry Research and Brownstone Research were the two largest companies MarketWise owned.
It calculated $37 million in net effective cash and said net billings were up in the recent quarter.
Ragnarok Research set a price target of $25 to $30 for MarketWise and noted a $50 million buyback.
body: MarketWise is an owner of companies that publish research and due diligence primarily for retail investors. In mid-2024, the company began shutting down a unit called Legacy Research, and its stock fell from about $60 to about $20.

On July 24, 2025, Ragnarok Research published a report on MarketWise and disclosed that it held a long position in the stock. The firm analyzed web traffic data and found that Stansberry Research and Brownstone Research were the two largest companies MarketWise owned.

Ragnarok Research stated that MarketWise generated $83 million in revenue in the most recent quarter and held $79 million in cash against $457 million in total liabilities and $415 million in total deferred revenue. It calculated $37 million in net effective cash and said net billings were up in the recent quarter.
Ragnarok Research set a price target of $25 to $30 for MarketWise and noted a $50 million buyback.

title: Flux Power had negative $4.3 million in book value a week before a Nasdaq deadline
points: Sunshine Research wrote that Flux Power had reported a negative book value of $4.3 million on March 31, 2025, leaving a $6.8 million gap.
To cover 4 to 8 quarters of ongoing operating losses, the investigator estimated the company needed to raise $14.6 million to $22.3 million, equal to 30% to 65% of its market cap.
By the end of that week, the share price had fallen 11%, from $2.06 to $1.83, as investors weighed the compliance deadline and possible dilution.
body: Flux Power Holdings is a US manufacturer of lithium-ion battery systems for forklifts and airport ground support equipment. It buys battery cells from China, assembles them into packs, and sells them to equipment makers.

On July 23, 2025, Sunshine Research published a report saying Flux Power was an attractive short. It noted that on February 3, 2025, Flux Power had disclosed falling below the Nasdaq minimum of $2.5 million in stockholder equity, with a compliance extension expiring on July 30, 2025.

Sunshine Research wrote that Flux Power had reported a negative book value of $4.3 million on March 31, 2025, leaving a $6.8 million gap. To cover 4 to 8 quarters of ongoing operating losses, the investigator estimated the company needed to raise $14.6 million to $22.3 million, equal to 30% to 65% of its market cap.

On July 23, 2025, the shares dipped to $1.97 intraday and closed at $2.12. By the end of that week, the share price had fallen 11%, from $2.06 to $1.83, as investors weighed the compliance deadline and possible dilution.

title: Aether listed on Nasdaq with $3,000 in equipment and a 235-square-foot virtual office
points: BMF Reports said Aether's filings claimed no material relationship with 28 Ventures and omitted that FINRA had permanently barred Cid in January 2022.
The report also said Aether had only a $12K-a-year virtual office of 235 square feet and less than $3,000 in net property and equipment.
Shareholder law firms Robbins LLP and Johnson Fistel announced investigations into Aether in June and October 2026 over possible securities law violations.
body: Aether Holdings, Inc. operates a financial technology platform in the United States. It listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market in April 2025, raising about $8.901 million in its initial public offering.

On July 23, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published a report on Aether. It alleged that Chief Executive Officer Nicolas Lin and business development head Frank Cid used a shell entity, 28 Ventures Aether, to sell 428,572 shares right after the offering despite a lock-up clause.

BMF Reports said Aether's filings claimed no material relationship with 28 Ventures and omitted that FINRA had permanently barred Cid in January 2022. The report also said Aether had only a $12K-a-year virtual office of 235 square feet and less than $3,000 in net property and equipment.
Shareholder law firms Robbins LLP and Johnson Fistel announced investigations into Aether in June and October 2026 over possible securities law violations.

title: A short seller said Limbach Holdings overstated free cash flow by 200%
points: Spruce Point alleged that Limbach overstated its adjusted EBITDA by 13% and its free cash flow by 200% over the last twelve months.
The report also alleged that Limbach's acquisitions failed to stop revenue loss, organic growth was slowing, and financial disclosures had grown opaque.
Spruce Point estimated 20% to 50% potential downside risk for the shares, setting a target range of $62.00 to $99.00 per share.
body: Limbach Holdings designs and maintains HVAC, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure. The company went public through a SPAC transaction in 2016 and held unanimous Buy ratings from sell-side analysts with an average price target of $141.50 per share.

On July 22, 2025, short seller Spruce Point Capital Management published a report following a forensic financial review and disclosed a short position in the stock. Spruce Point alleged that Limbach overstated its adjusted EBITDA by 13% and its free cash flow by 200% over the last twelve months.

The report also alleged that Limbach's acquisitions failed to stop revenue loss, organic growth was slowing, and financial disclosures had grown opaque. Spruce Point pointed to board links to an Enron spin-off, Qwest Communications, and Granite Construction, and noted a past fiduciary duty lawsuit against the chief financial officer.
Spruce Point estimated 20% to 50% potential downside risk for the shares, setting a target range of $62.00 to $99.00 per share.

title: Enovis Claimed 6-10% Organic Growth. A Short Seller Calculated 2%.
points: Jehoshaphat held a short position, which meant it stood to profit if Enovis shares fell.
Against the company's stated 6-10%, Jehoshaphat arrived at 2%.
It said Enovis had generated negative free cash flow in aggregate for 20 years under different owners and managers.
body: Enovis Corporation is a US medical technology company focused on orthopedic products. It told investors that sales from its existing business grew organically by 6-10%, meaning growth apart from acquisitions. Analysts had seen the company meet quarterly earnings estimates for ten years.

On July 17, 2025, Jehoshaphat Research published a report alleging that Enovis had inflated its organic revenue growth and profits for years. Jehoshaphat held a short position, which meant it stood to profit if Enovis shares fell.

The investigator said it examined irregularities in Enovis's reported figures and recalculated organic growth by hand. Against the company's stated 6-10%, Jehoshaphat arrived at 2%. The report argued that repeated acquisitions had helped support the company's reported performance while debt had reached a level that would restrict further deals.

Jehoshaphat also challenged Enovis's adjusted EBITDA and predicted that the company would continue generating negative free cash flow. It said Enovis had generated negative free cash flow in aggregate for 20 years under different owners and managers.
The CEO who had overseen Enovis's acquisition program had resigned the previous quarter. That resignation preceded the short seller's report.

title: Alset had $20 million in cash and a $13 million market value
points: It put the company's market value at $13 million and cash holdings at about $20 million.
The report cited those sales and share purchases by Alset's CEO earlier in 2025 as reasons to expect better shareholder returns.
The July 15, 2025 report argued that Alset's cash and properties supported a higher share valuation and that buybacks could benefit shareholders.
body: Alset Inc (AEI) had moved from building and installing solar homes into residential real estate. Its earlier business involved Tesla, but the arrangement either failed to develop or ended as Alset changed direction. Its shares had fallen from their 2021 levels.

On July 15, 2025, Ragnarok Research published a report arguing that Alset's shares were undervalued. It put the company's market value at $13 million and cash holdings at about $20 million. Alset's first-quarter 2025 financial statements showed about $25 million in cash.

Ragnarok Research also identified about 132 single-family homes owned by Alset. A subsidiary had sold residential properties for $4 million in late 2024. The report cited those sales and share purchases by Alset's CEO earlier in 2025 as reasons to expect better shareholder returns.

Ragnarok Research disclosed a long position, meaning it stood to gain if Alset's shares rose. It blamed the weak share price on the shift into real estate, limited trading and a complicated company structure. The report recommended buying shares rather than alleging fraud.

The July 15, 2025 report argued that Alset's cash and properties supported a higher share valuation and that buybacks could benefit shareholders. The $13 million was Alset's market value, not a financial loss.

title: UnitedHealth Group faced a federal probe and a pharmacy rebate inquiry.
points: The company said it had proactively reached out to the Justice Department after news reports of a government investigation surfaced.
Hunterbrook said its investment affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, held no positions related to the article at publication.
The latest dated event in the reporting was Hunterbrook Media's November 11, 2026 publication noting that its affiliate Hunterbrook Law was working with a litigation firm on potential legal claims.
body: UnitedHealth Group is a United States health care conglomerate that owns insurer UnitedHealthcare, care network Optum, and pharmacy benefit manager Optum Rx. It reported $400.3 billion in full-year revenue for 2024 and told investors its scale helped integrate care and maintain integrity in its business practices.

On July 24, 2025, UnitedHealth announced it was cooperating with a U.S. Justice Department probe into its Medicare Advantage plans. The company said it had proactively reached out to the Justice Department after news reports of a government investigation surfaced.

On November 11, 2026, Hunterbrook Media reported that UnitedHealth, CVS Health, and Cigna created pharmacy benefit manager group purchasing organizations to divert billions of dollars from health plans and patients. Hunterbrook interviewed executives and former staffers, analyzed data, visited offices from Ireland to Switzerland, and reviewed thousands of pages of contracts and court records.

Hunterbrook said its investment affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, held no positions related to the article at publication. The latest dated event in the reporting was Hunterbrook Media's November 11, 2026 publication noting that its affiliate Hunterbrook Law was working with a litigation firm on potential legal claims.

title: Joby Aviation burned $477 million in nine months while trading at $9.5 billion
points: Short seller Abelian Analysis published a report cross-referencing Joby's SEC filings, USPTO patents, engineering literature, and FAA documents.
The report said Joby traded at a $9.5 billion market capitalization without ever flying a paying passenger, and held a short position on the stock, which earns when shares fall.
Abelian Analysis alleged that Joby reported $22.6 million in revenue against $477 million in operating cash burn through the first three quarters of 2025.
body: Joby Aviation is a California-based aerospace company developing electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft and hydrogen-powered unmanned aerial vehicles. It told investors it aimed to certify its S4 battery-electric air taxi, acquire revenue, and begin Dubai operations in early 2026.

On February 22, 2026, short seller Abelian Analysis published a report cross-referencing Joby's SEC filings, USPTO patents, engineering literature, and FAA documents. The report said Joby traded at a $9.5 billion market capitalization without ever flying a paying passenger, and held a short position on the stock, which earns when shares fall.

Abelian Analysis alleged that Joby reported $22.6 million in revenue against $477 million in operating cash burn through the first three quarters of 2025. It said Joby held $978 million in cash and short-term investments as of September 30, 2025, and raised about $785 million across four equity offerings since the second quarter of 2023, increasing shares outstanding by 39% from 630 million to 874 million.

On June 26, 2026, Hunterbrook Media reported that its affiliate Hunterbrook Capital was long Joby shares after reporters observed Joby testing a hydrogen-powered unmanned aircraft, the JAI 30, for at least nine hours at Pendleton Airport on June 30, 2025.

title: Vedanta diverted ₹3,247 crore in brand fees to its parent company
points: The investigator alleged that ₹3,247 crore in brand fees were diverted to Vedanta Resources despite no clear services rendered.
The investigator stated that Vedanta previously agreed to rebate ₹1,030 crore to Vedanta Limited to avoid enforcement action.
An incident at Vedanta's Chhattisgarh Athena Power Plant led to the death of at least 20 workers and over 36 workers injured.
body: Vedanta Limited is an Indian company that operates in mining and industrial sectors, and it told investors that its business was growing while generating record earnings.

The short-seller Viceroy Research published a report stating that the company was systematically drained by its largest shareholder, Vedanta Resources Limited, and the Agarwal family. The investigator alleged that ₹3,247 crore in brand fees were diverted to Vedanta Resources despite no clear services rendered.

The report stated that whenever the parent company faced a liquidity crunch, it triggered ad hoc remittances from Vedanta Limited under the banner of brand fees. The investigator stated that Vedanta previously agreed to rebate ₹1,030 crore to Vedanta Limited to avoid enforcement action.

On April 14, 2026, an incident at Vedanta's Chhattisgarh Athena Power Plant led to the death of at least 20 workers and over 36 workers injured. Viceroy reported that the government announced Indian taxpayers would fund bereavement payments to the families of the victims.

investigator: The Equity Dispatch, J Capital Research
title: Transcat traded at 56 times trailing earnings while growing like an industrial firm.
points: The report alleged that Transcat kept buying companies at very high prices while realizing few synergies.
It stated that the stock attracted a tech company multiple of 56x trailing earnings even though the business was growing like an old-time industrial company.
The short seller published the report on July 9, 2025, questioning why investors paid that multiple for the stock.
body: Transcat is a Nasdaq-listed company that sells, rents, and calibrates measuring equipment for the pharmaceutical, aerospace, utilities, and oilfield industries. It dispatches a fleet of vans to client sites to adjust their instruments and has grown through acquiring other firms.
On July 9, 2025, J Capital Research published a report under The Equity Dispatch examining Transcat's acquisition strategy and valuation.

The report alleged that Transcat kept buying companies at very high prices while realizing few synergies. It stated that the stock attracted a tech company multiple of 56x trailing earnings even though the business was growing like an old-time industrial company.
The short seller published the report on July 9, 2025, questioning why investors paid that multiple for the stock.

title: Hindustan Zinc shares fell 4.8% as Viceroy alleged cash was drained
points: On July 9, Hindustan Zinc shares fell 4.8% to Rs 415.30, while Vedanta Limited shares fell as much as 7.7% to Rs 421.
On August 25, it reported that Hindustan Zinc had paid ₹1,060 crore ($121m) in Brand and Strategic Services fees to Vedanta Limited in Q1 FY26, which was then remitted to Vedanta Resources.
It said the payment represented a 61% increase over the previous year.
body: Hindustan Zinc is a subsidiary of Vedanta Limited, part of the Vedanta group. On July 9, 2025, short-seller Viceroy Research challenged the group's finances and alleged that its parent company depended on cash extracted from operating businesses.

Viceroy alleged that Vedanta Resources Limited took cash from Vedanta Limited to service its own debt, forcing the operating company to borrow more. The report described the group structure as financially unsustainable and alleged material discrepancies in its finances.

On July 9, Hindustan Zinc shares fell 4.8% to Rs 415.30, while Vedanta Limited shares fell as much as 7.7% to Rs 421. These were share-price movements, not amounts of cash allegedly transferred. Viceroy disclosed that its financial interests could benefit from falling security prices.

Viceroy continued publishing allegations about Hindustan Zinc. On August 25, it reported that Hindustan Zinc had paid ₹1,060 crore ($121m) in Brand and Strategic Services fees to Vedanta Limited in Q1 FY26, which was then remitted to Vedanta Resources. It said the payment represented a 61% increase over the previous year.

On October 23, Viceroy reported that Vedanta Resources had disclosed in its September 30, 2025 bond prospectus that the group had received summons from SEBI based on Viceroy's research. The disclosure established that the securities regulator had issued summons, not that Viceroy's allegations had been proven.

title: Bitmine Immersion raised $250 million to buy Ethereum while holding zero tokens
points: Fugazi Research alleged that Bitmine held zero Ethereum tokens while its stock soared over 2,500% to $160 per share on a float of 3.2 million shares.
The report said the 55 million insider shares included full resale rights and noted that the chief executive's private company owned the mining rigs and took 88% of the Bitcoin produced.
Kerrisdale also alleged that a $365 million direct offering promoted as accretive at $70 per share was actually a discount once attached warrants were counted.
body: Bitmine Immersion Technologies is a Las Vegas-based digital-asset company that previously mined Bitcoin and told investors it was becoming a large Ethereum treasury vehicle. On June 30, 2025, the company announced a $250 million private placement of 55 million shares at $4.50 each to fund Ethereum purchases.

On July 9, 2025, Fugazi Research alleged that Bitmine held zero Ethereum tokens while its stock soared over 2,500% to $160 per share on a float of 3.2 million shares. The report said the 55 million insider shares included full resale rights and noted that the chief executive's private company owned the mining rigs and took 88% of the Bitcoin produced.

On October 8, 2025, Kerrisdale Capital published a report and said it held a short position, earning if the stock fell. Kerrisdale alleged that Bitmine had issued more than $10 billion in new stock over three months, or about $170 million per day, to accumulate over 2.8 million tokens while stopping weekly share-count updates.

Kerrisdale also alleged that a $365 million direct offering promoted as accretive at $70 per share was actually a discount once attached warrants were counted. Bitmine shares fell 2% on October 8, 2025.

On March 5, 2026, Culper Research wrote that Bitmine, led by chairman Tom Lee, was overwhelmingly responsible for driving Ethereum staking demand, with the staking entry queue sitting at 3.35 million tokens.

title: 86 servers and 588 subscription sellers leaked fleet data through Uffizio software
points: The investigator stated that Uffizio software and its deployment by hundreds of global resellers leaked sensitive fleet data across at least 12 countries for over five years.
The investigator found 86 IP addresses with JSON files and 588 subscription selling companies selling Uffizio products under their own brand.
The investigator noted that a CISA Advisory was published on October 18, 2021, affecting equipment referred to as Uffizio GPS Tracker, vulnerable to five vulnerabilities.
body: Uffizio is a software company in India that provides a GPS tracking software service supporting over 1,200 trackers and managing data sent by GPS trackers produced by various manufacturers. The company told investors and the public that it was GDPR compliant.

On July 7, 2025, Deep Specter Research published a report stating that it uncovered a multi-year data exposure involving Uffizio. The investigator stated that Uffizio software and its deployment by hundreds of global resellers leaked sensitive fleet data across at least 12 countries for over five years.

The report said that the exposure continued even after a public CVE disclosure and an internal GDPR audit. The investigator found 86 IP addresses with JSON files and 588 subscription selling companies selling Uffizio products under their own brand.

The investigator noted that a CISA Advisory was published on October 18, 2021, affecting equipment referred to as Uffizio GPS Tracker, vulnerable to five vulnerabilities. The report also stated that an internal GDPR audit by Uffizio was completed on June 30, 2021, and that leaks continued until 2022, with some servers managed by Uffizio resuming leaks in 2023.

title: Eutelsat carried 3 billion euros in net debt. A short seller saw a 70% drop.
points: HitHawk presented a short case for the stock, meaning it would earn money if the shares fell.
The report also raised concerns about the company's 3 billion euros of net debt.
HitHawk issued a price target that implied about 70% downside for the shares.
body: Eutelsat Communications is a European satellite company listed in Paris under the ticker ETL. Its shares had recently rallied on expectations around a new chief executive and a capital injection from France.
On July 6, 2025, HitHawk Research published a report on the company. HitHawk presented a short case for the stock, meaning it would earn money if the shares fell.

HitHawk alleged that Eutelsat lagged far behind competitors such as Starlink and Kuiper in technology, scale, and innovation. The report also raised concerns about the company's 3 billion euros of net debt.

HitHawk issued a price target that implied about 70% downside for the shares. The debt and the price target are different types of figures - one is money the company owed, and the other is an estimate of where the stock could trade.

title: Carrefour reported €8.8 billion in net debt. An activist fund said it was €10.4 billion.
points: Whitelight Capital held an undisclosed stake in Carrefour, and shares rose 0.27% to 13.3 euros that day.
Whitelight Capital founder Kevin Romanteau alleged that Carrefour used accounting maneuvers to hide at least €1.5 billion in debt.
He said net debt was actually €10.4 billion rather than €8.8 billion and threatened legal action against board members.
body: Carrefour is a French supermarket group led by CEO Alexandre Bompard. It reported €8.8 billion in net debt.

On March 10, 2025, France-based activist fund Whitelight Capital warned that rising tensions with Carrefour franchise stores in France created structural risks for shareholders. The Carrefour Franchisees Association, which represents 260 stores, had launched an alternative purchasing network named Project X and had previously sued Carrefour over product prices. Whitelight Capital held an undisclosed stake in Carrefour, and shares rose 0.27% to 13.3 euros that day.

On July 4, 2025, Whitelight Capital founder Kevin Romanteau alleged that Carrefour used accounting maneuvers to hide at least €1.5 billion in debt. He said net debt was actually €10.4 billion rather than €8.8 billion and threatened legal action against board members. Romanteau also suggested that delisting Carrefour's Brazilian branch could allow the operations to continue more discreetly.
An internal source at Carrefour rejected the accusation. The source pointed to the company's BBB rating from Standard & Poor's and said factoring was a well-known practice disclosed in the accounts.

title: BCG modelled relocating Palestinians from Gaza under a multimillion-dollar contract
points: Chief executive Christoph Schweizer stated that the Gaza work was disavowed and partners exited the firm.
Boston Consulting Group announced the results of an investigation it had commissioned.
The firm said some of its U.S.-based staff had sidestepped its risk controls to do work related to the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation and post-war reconstruction for Gaza.
body: Boston Consulting Group is a consulting firm.

On July 4, 2025, the Financial Times reported that Boston Consulting Group had modelled the costs of relocating Palestinians from Gaza. The newspaper also reported that the firm entered into a multimillion-dollar contract to help launch an aid scheme for Gaza and advised the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation and Safe Reach Solutions on their operations there.
Chief executive Christoph Schweizer stated that the Gaza work was disavowed and partners exited the firm.

On July 24, 2025, Boston Consulting Group announced the results of an investigation it had commissioned. The firm said some of its U.S.-based staff had sidestepped its risk controls to do work related to the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation and post-war reconstruction for Gaza.

title: Nutex Took a $55 Million Charge for Arbitration Claims It Could Not Collect
points: On November 26, Nutex challenged the short seller's credibility, saying Capybara Research appeared not to exist as an identifiable entity.
On December 16, Capybara published a second report alleging that former employees had described pressure from Vo to improperly code medical bills and overcharge insurers.
Capybara said Nutex had taken a $55 million charge for arbitration claims the company determined were ineligible for reimbursement.
body: Nutex Health is a Houston-based healthcare company that operates emergency rooms and small hospitals. It reported third-quarter revenue of $268 million and adjusted EBITDA of $105 million. The company operated 24 facilities across 11 states.

On November 25, 2025, Capybara Research published an investigation based on interviews with former insiders and business partners. It alleged that founder and CEO Thomas Vo had engaged in fraud, embezzlement and self-dealing. Capybara said Nutex had been removed from more than a dozen emergency rooms.

On November 26, Nutex challenged the short seller's credibility, saying Capybara Research appeared not to exist as an identifiable entity. On December 16, Capybara published a second report alleging that former employees had described pressure from Vo to improperly code medical bills and overcharge insurers.

On October 15, 2026, Capybara said Nutex had taken a $55 million charge for arbitration claims the company determined were ineligible for reimbursement. Capybara had previously alleged that such claims inflated receivables. The charge concerned amounts Nutex could not collect, not money stolen. Capybara, which disclosed a short position, said the shares fell over 20% on the news. Its affiliates stood to profit from a falling share price.

title: A Dutch hotel broker received over €400 million and earned nearly €45 million
points: LCHD earned nearly €45 million by taking both large margins and commissions on the hotel bookings.
Since the summer of 2023, the Dutch Public Prosecution Service has investigated Derksen as a suspect for fraud and possible unlawfully obtained gains.
The COA is demanding €184,7 million from Derksen and LCHD, which is separate from the €400 million received and the €45 million earned.
body: LCHD is a Dutch intermediary company owned by René Derksen that arranged temporary hotel rooms and halls for asylum seekers on behalf of the Dutch asylum agency COA. Between early 2022 and mid-2024, LCHD received more than €400 million to rent rooms and halls.

Het Financieele Dagblad examined contracts between LCHD, the COA and hotel chains such as Van der Valk and Fletcher. LCHD earned nearly €45 million by taking both large margins and commissions on the hotel bookings.

Derksen denied wrongdoing and said the price agreements were transparent and the cooperation with the COA went smoothly. The COA terminated its contract with LCHD over an alleged breach of obligations.

Since the summer of 2023, the Dutch Public Prosecution Service has investigated Derksen as a suspect for fraud and possible unlawfully obtained gains. The COA is demanding €184,7 million from Derksen and LCHD, which is separate from the €400 million received and the €45 million earned.

title: Kinsale shares rose 1,560% since 2016. Short sellers said its policies relied on exclusions.
points: It later reported that gross premiums written declined 3.5% year-over-year compared to the same period in 2025.
He filed public record requests and obtained customer complaints sent to insurance regulators alleging overcharges, improper billing, and ineffective coverage.
One commentator noted the share price had fallen 35% since PAA Research's July 2025 publication.
body: Kinsale Capital Group is a specialty property-and-casualty insurer listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It sells coverage for unusual or hard-to-place risks, and its stock rose about 1,560% after its July 2016 initial public offering.

In July 2025, short seller PAA Research published a report setting a $230 price objective on the shares. It later reported that gross premiums written declined 3.5% year-over-year compared to the same period in 2025.

On May 7, 2026, Edwin Dorsey published a report on The Bear Cave. He filed public record requests and obtained customer complaints sent to insurance regulators alleging overcharges, improper billing, and ineffective coverage.

The Bear Cave alleged that Kinsale relied on overpriced, exclusion-heavy policies and minimal regulatory oversight rather than superior underwriting. By May 24, 2026, one commentator noted the share price had fallen 35% since PAA Research's July 2025 publication.

title: INmune Bio issued 600,000 shares to a consultant using a virtual shell office
points: The report said INmune Bio built its valuation on an abandoned drug and selective quotes from unblinded observations rather than sound science.
BMF Reports also alleged that INmune Bio paid 600,000 restricted shares priced at $2.50 to a consulting entity using a virtual shell office in Vancouver, Canada, and a fake LinkedIn identity.
INmune Bio had reported a $42.1 million net loss in 2024, up from $30 million the previous year.
body: INmune Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company listed on Nasdaq. It told investors its lead drug candidate, XPro1595, could treat neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.

On June 27, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published an investigation into the company's trial design and filings. The report said INmune Bio built its valuation on an abandoned drug and selective quotes from unblinded observations rather than sound science.

BMF Reports also alleged that INmune Bio paid 600,000 restricted shares priced at $2.50 to a consulting entity using a virtual shell office in Vancouver, Canada, and a fake LinkedIn identity. It added that SEC filings showed repeated stock, option, and cash payments to consulting entities that appeared to vanish outside of Edgar.
INmune Bio had reported a $42.1 million net loss in 2024, up from $30 million the previous year.

title: Lennar beat its delivery forecast by 340 homes after its spinoff bought 356
points: By checking county records and Zillow listings, Hunterbrook identified more than 700 Millrose purchases across 15 states, worth an estimated $200 million or more in about a month.
Hunterbrook estimated the rented homes would return about 5% a year before interest, below Millrose's 6.5% to 6.75% bond rates.
Hunterbrook reported that reporters visited 36 Millrose houses in Florida and 39 in Texas and found more than 95% of analyzed purchases advertised for rent.
body: Lennar is America's second-largest homebuilder. In 2025, it spun off Millrose Properties to hold land for future construction, with Lennar CEO Stuart Miller as Millrose's largest voting shareholder. Lennar told investors that weak numbers came from soft demand and deliberate price cuts.

On October 2, 2026, Hunterbrook Media reported that Millrose had changed its agreements in August to buy Lennar's finished homes, while affiliate Hunterbrook Capital held short positions in both stocks. By checking county records and Zillow listings, Hunterbrook identified more than 700 Millrose purchases across 15 states, worth an estimated $200 million or more in about a month.

The report said at least 356 of those purchases closed in the final week of Lennar's third fiscal quarter, helping Lennar beat its delivery forecast by 340 homes. Hunterbrook estimated the rented homes would return about 5% a year before interest, below Millrose's 6.5% to 6.75% bond rates.

Millrose told Goldman Sachs it bought homes with signed leases already in place. On October 8, 2026, Hunterbrook reported that reporters visited 36 Millrose houses in Florida and 39 in Texas and found more than 95% of analyzed purchases advertised for rent.

title: D.R. Horton faced 198 South Carolina court complaints over 10 years
points: It found 198 complaints filed against D.R.
Horton in South Carolina county courts over 10 years, and noted that contracts required private arbitration.
A law firm told Hunterbrook that about 500 South Carolina homeowners had contacted it with complaints, with 125 cases under investigation.
body: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States. The company remained profitable even as its stock price fell more than 30% in the previous year amid cooling demand and rising costs.

Hunterbrook Media interviewed homeowners, former employees, and building experts, and reviewed purchase agreements, warranty policies, and court records. Its investment affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, held no position in the company at publication.

Hunterbrook alleged that the builder cut corners, discouraged third-party inspections, and pushed repair costs onto buyers. It found 198 complaints filed against D.R. Horton in South Carolina county courts over 10 years, and noted that contracts required private arbitration.

On June 26, 2025, Hunterbrook published its report and said it was working with litigators on potential lawsuits. A law firm told Hunterbrook that about 500 South Carolina homeowners had contacted it with complaints, with 125 cases under investigation.

title: Capricor shares fell over 15%. Its lead treatment still lacked FDA approval.
points: Capricor shares fell over 15% that Monday, reaching an intraday low of $4.74 against Friday's closing price of $5.75.
Shkreli predicted a decline toward approximately $2 per share.
Instead, the agency had agreed to review additional 24-month data for the treatment.
body: Capricor Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company developing cell-based treatments for rare diseases. Its lead treatment, Deramiocel, targets Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a disease affecting fewer than 20,000 young boys in the United States. The company promoted promising clinical results and long-term improvements in patients.

On June 26, 2025, BMF Reports accused Capricor of using the disease to attract tens of millions in taxpayer-funded grants and money from retail investors. The report alleged that clinical trials suffered repeated delays, changing endpoints and extended studies while insiders benefited financially. It also questioned whether Capricor had submitted adequate pharmacologic evidence for Deramiocel.

On November 24, 2025, Martin Shkreli publicly identified Capricor as a short target. He questioned whether its cell therapy could reach diseased tissue and challenged the company's interpretation of HOPE-2 trial results, saying the FDA disagreed with its assessment.

Capricor shares fell over 15% that Monday, reaching an intraday low of $4.74 against Friday's closing price of $5.75. Shkreli predicted a decline toward approximately $2 per share. Capricor separately announced findings about its exosome technology, which Chief Executive Linda Marbán said supported its potential across multiple diseases.
The FDA had not approved Deramiocel. Instead, the agency had agreed to review additional 24-month data for the treatment. Capricor's shares had moved higher following that decision.

title: Worldline handled 500 billion euros a year. Reporters found 580 high-fee merchants.
points: Mediapart and 20 other media outlets in the European Investigative Collaborations network examined confidential Worldline documents.
According to the report, more than 580 e-merchants paid over 5% in commission.
Worldline shares fell more than a third after the June 2025 report.
body: Worldline is a French payment processor that handles 500 billion euros in card transactions each year. The company told investors it had strengthened merchant risk controls and ended non-compliant client ties since 2023.

In June 2025, Mediapart and 20 other media outlets in the European Investigative Collaborations network examined confidential Worldline documents. The outlets alleged that Worldline processed billions of euros in fraudulent payments for online scammers and illegal casinos over ten years.

According to the report, more than 580 e-merchants paid over 5% in commission. The outlets also stated that after German regulator BaFin banned Worldline unit Payone from working with 450 clients in 2023, Worldline kept serving hundreds of them through other units.
Worldline shares fell more than a third after the June 2025 report. The company stated it would cooperate with authorities.

Fewer than three days after the initial publication, Belgian prosecutors opened a money laundering investigation into Worldline's Belgian unit. On November 6, 2025, Mediapart reported that Payone was named in German court proceedings involving online fraud networks.

title: Microvast reported up to 250 staff at a German plant. Investigators found fewer than 30 cars.
points: It said 39 of 41 random checks at the German plant showed almost no truck traffic and fewer than 30 cars on average in the parking lot.
It also alleged the China factory employed about 1,400 people and that more than 95% of non-Chinese clients were tiny startups.
Microvast had previously been denied a $200 million U.S. government grant over suspected Chinese government ties, which management denied.
body: Microvast Holdings is a Texas-based battery maker listed on Nasdaq. It told investors it had hundreds of millions in revenue, up to 250 workers at a plant near Berlin and over 2,500 at a factory in China.

On June 25, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report after visiting the sites and checking satellite images. It said 39 of 41 random checks at the German plant showed almost no truck traffic and fewer than 30 cars on average in the parking lot. It also alleged the China factory employed about 1,400 people and that more than 95% of non-Chinese clients were tiny startups.

Grizzly Research further alleged that the Chinese government held a stake in Microvast's main Chinese unit. Microvast had previously been denied a $200 million U.S. government grant over suspected Chinese government ties, which management denied.

Microvast shares fell 7% that Wednesday, dropping as much as $0.40, or 10.23%, during trading before closing at $3.90. On August 1, 2025, Microvast announced that Chief Financial Officer Charles Schultz was leaving after three months. On September 2, 2026, a law firm announced a shareholder class action lawsuit covering shares bought through March 16, 2026.

title: CTO Realty Growth had a $38 million dividend shortfall and raised share count by 70%
points: The report alleged that CTO excluded recurring capital expenditures from its Adjusted Funds From Operation metric, which also determined 70% of management's performance pay.
Wolfpack alleged that CTO had a $38 million dividend shortfall from 2021 to 2024 and increased its shares outstanding by 70% since December 2022 to cover it.
The report further alleged that CTO did not impair a loan after a tenant stopped paying rent in November 2022 and an affiliate and its owner filed for bankruptcy in early 2023.
body: CTO Realty Growth is a real estate investment trust listed on the New York Stock Exchange that buys and manages shopping centers. It told investors about its dividend sustainability and used an Adjusted Funds From Operation metric.

On June 25, 2025, short seller Wolfpack Research published a report analyzing the company and its proxy filings, and said it held a short position in the stock. The report alleged that CTO excluded recurring capital expenditures from its Adjusted Funds From Operation metric, which also determined 70% of management's performance pay.

Wolfpack alleged that CTO had a $38 million dividend shortfall from 2021 to 2024 and increased its shares outstanding by 70% since December 2022 to cover it. The report also alleged CTO held $8.4 million in cash against $14 million in quarterly dividends, $5.7 million in average quarterly recurring capital expenditures, and about $12 million in additional planned capital expenditures.

The report further alleged that CTO did not impair a loan after a tenant stopped paying rent in November 2022 and an affiliate and its owner filed for bankruptcy in early 2023. CTO shares fell 3.7% on June 25, 2025.

title: Johns Lyng paid subsidiaries more than 100% of their profits
points: Crash Capital argued that the estimates were too high because insurers checked invoices closely, and pointed to the company's dealings with Suncorp in FY'24.
On June 24, Crash Capital examined how Johns Lyng financed acquisitions.
The resulting structure involved about 200 entities, while payouts to non-controlling interests exceeded 100% of their share of profits.
body: Johns Lyng Group is an Australian business that buys building restoration contractors and handles insurance repair work. It held about 8% of a fragmented market and used its ability to respond to major weather events to secure routine work from insurers. Investors had valued its shares at around 25 times earnings on expectations of additional revenue from cross-selling services.

On April 21, 2025, Crash Capital alleged that Johns Lyng recognised revenue too early. The company estimated the costs insurers would reimburse, measured work completed against those estimates and recorded revenue before receiving payment. Crash Capital argued that the estimates were too high because insurers checked invoices closely, and pointed to the company's dealings with Suncorp in FY'24.

On June 24, Crash Capital examined how Johns Lyng financed acquisitions. It said the parent company lent money to contractors so they could retain equity in businesses they had sold. The resulting structure involved about 200 entities, while payouts to non-controlling interests exceeded 100% of their share of profits.

Crash Capital also alleged that the parent bought and sold small subsidiary stakes to maintain equity balances. As business slowed, the parent absorbed a larger share of the profit decline than minority owners. Johns Lyng entered a trading halt to announce that it had received an offer, without disclosing its value.

title: A short activist pointed to a 1936 seizure at perfume retailer Douglas AG
points: HitHawk described Douglas AG as a legacy retailer in decline with unsustainable debt, reliance on shrinking high-street traffic and a weak digital presence.
HitHawk also alleged that the perfumery that became Douglas was likely seized from Jewish owners in 1936 and handed to a Nazi-approved businessman.
The report said the company faces potential legal claims for restitution and reputational damage.
body: Douglas AG is a large German perfume and beauty retailer listed in Frankfurt under the ticker DOU with a market value of EUR1.17 billion. Its shares had fallen about 50% since its March 2024 initial public offering.

On June 15, 2025, Europe-focused short activist HitHawk Research published a report on the company. HitHawk described Douglas AG as a legacy retailer in decline with unsustainable debt, reliance on shrinking high-street traffic and a weak digital presence.

HitHawk also alleged that the perfumery that became Douglas was likely seized from Jewish owners in 1936 and handed to a Nazi-approved businessman. The report said the company faces potential legal claims for restitution and reputational damage.

title: The RealReal sold used luxury goods. Its checks allegedly let fakes through.
points: The firm alleged that The RealReal's authentication process let through many counterfeit products.
It said the problem had angered both buyers and sellers and damaged their trust in the company.
The researchers said they found no evidence that the technology was effective.
body: The RealReal is a Nasdaq-listed company that sells used luxury goods. Its business depends on checking whether those goods are genuine before selling them to buyers. Customers rely on those checks when deciding whether to buy.

On June 11, 2025, J Capital Research published a short report questioning those checks. The firm alleged that The RealReal's authentication process let through many counterfeit products. It said the problem had angered both buyers and sellers and damaged their trust in the company.

J Capital also examined the company's use of artificial intelligence to speed up authentication. The researchers said they found no evidence that the technology was effective. They argued that The RealReal handled too many different kinds of products for its authenticators to receive adequate training.

The report questioned whether the business could operate profitably while keeping counterfeit goods out. J Capital argued that processing enough products to become profitable would inevitably allow fakes through. The allegation concerned the reliability of authentication, not a stated amount of financial loss.
The report appeared on June 11, 2025. J Capital's published assessment was that The RealReal's business model might not work because of the difficulty of authenticating goods at scale.

title: Yorkville sought $150 million for a SPAC after years of regulatory fines

body: Yorkville Acquisition Corp. is a blank-check company sponsored by Yorkville Advisors Global, LP. It filed an amended prospectus to raise $150 million in an initial public offering at $10.00 per unit.

On June 10, 2025, short-selling research platform Shortfinder published a report on the offering. Shortfinder said Yorkville Advisors manages offshore hedge funds that buy discounted stock, warrants, and convertible debt from small companies and sell the shares into public markets, which often pushes down stock prices.

Shortfinder also listed past regulatory actions against Yorkville Advisors. In 2011, Italian regulators fined Yorkville and its chairman for breaking takeover rules, and in 2012, the SEC sued Yorkville over allegations that it reported false and inflated values for certain securities.

In May 2022, Yorkville settled a Swiss investigation into alleged reporting failures on derivative holdings in three Swiss-listed companies. The Tax Court also sided with the IRS in a separate dispute, which Yorkville is appealing.

title: Groupon touted $40.6 million in free cash flow before a short seller questioned its books
points: The report accused Groupon of using dubious accounting methods and misleading investors about the success of its turnaround strategies.
Groupon shares dropped $1.61, or nearly 5%, that day to close at $31.33.
Law firm Pomerantz LLP announced an investigation into Groupon's business practices and the securities fraud claims raised by the report.
body: Groupon is a two-sided marketplace where consumers buy local deals and vouchers from merchants. In March 2025, the company told investors its turnaround was working, pointing to $40.6 million in positive free cash flow and 8% year-over-year growth in North America Local billings.

On June 9, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log published a report questioning those claims. The report accused Groupon of using dubious accounting methods and misleading investors about the success of its turnaround strategies.
Groupon shares dropped $1.61, or nearly 5%, that day to close at $31.33. The drop in share price reflects lost market value rather than cash taken from the company.
On June 22, 2025, law firm Pomerantz LLP announced an investigation into Groupon's business practices and the securities fraud claims raised by the report.

title: SharpLink announced a $425 million Ethereum pivot. SEC filings showed no holdings.

body: SharpLink Gaming is a Nasdaq-listed digital marketing firm that converts sports fans into bettors. In 2025, it announced a $425 million private placement led by ConsenSys to stockpile Ethereum.
On June 6, 2025, short seller Fugazi Research published a report on the company. Its affiliates or clients may hold short positions in the shares, earning money when the stock falls.

Fugazi Research checked SEC filings and blockchain records and said it found no Ethereum holdings or public wallet addresses tied to SharpLink. The report also noted a 1-for-12 reverse stock split on May 1, 2025, that cut the public float below 700,000 shares before a 4.5 million share offering on May 20, 2025.

The share price rose 4,000% during the Ethereum pivot and then fell 90.01% following the report. By July 9, 2025, Fugazi Research reported that SharpLink's float had expanded to over 70 million shares after insiders sold.

body: Newsmax, Inc. is a US public company that went public in April 2025. It reported a net loss of $8.4 million in the first quarter and held $15.1 million in cash as of March 31, 2025.

On June 6, 2025, research platform Shortfinder published a report examining SEC filings for Newsmax stock. Shortfinder pointed to two resale prospectuses declared effective by the SEC: one for 121.2 million shares held by more than 8,000 pre-IPO insiders, and another for up to 25.6 million Class B shares held by hedge fund YA II PN, Ltd.

The report noted that Newsmax would receive none of the proceeds from those resales and had a cash burn rate of $2.8 million per month, leaving a runway of five to six months. Exercising warrants would bring $13.3 million in cash while adding 6.9 million new shares to the market.
Newsmax shares fell 10% to close at $16.19 the day before the report, after dropping from nearly $20.00 earlier that week.

title: 61% of Abacus revenue came from gains on policies it still held
points: Morpheus Research published a 76-page report prepared over three months, with more than 400 citations and interviews with industry experts and former employees.
After adopting fair value accounting on June 30, 2023, Abacus reported $53.8 million in unrealized gains in 2024, representing 48% of revenue.
It said an outside actuarial firm, Lewis and Ellis, reviewed more than 700 policies without using Lapetus estimates.
body: Abacus Global Management is a US asset manager that buys and sells life insurance policies. It promoted returns of around 30% with little risk and described a potential market worth $233 billion.

On June 4, 2025, Morpheus Research published a 76-page report prepared over three months, with more than 400 citations and interviews with industry experts and former employees. Morpheus held a short position in Abacus shares, meaning it stood to profit if the price fell.

The report alleged that Abacus inflated revenue by raising the recorded value of policies it still owned. After adopting fair value accounting on June 30, 2023, Abacus reported $53.8 million in unrealized gains in 2024, representing 48% of revenue. By Q1 2025, such gains accounted for 61%. These were accounting gains, not cash received.

Morpheus questioned life expectancy estimates supplied by Lapetus Solutions, which affected policy valuations. Abacus rejected the report and threatened legal action. It said an outside actuarial firm, Lewis and Ellis, reviewed more than 700 policies without using Lapetus estimates.

On June 12, 2025, Morpheus published a follow-up disputing Abacus's response. It alleged undisclosed dealings with National Insurance Brokerage, an entity controlled by Abacus management, and challenged the company's explanation of its valuation methods.

title: A 49-slide presentation questioned Yalla Group's revenue and downloads
points: Short seller Pelican Way Research published a 49-slide presentation on the company.
Pelican Way compared Yalla's reported revenue metrics and downloads against third-party sources and its own calculations.
Two other firms, Akram's Razor and Swan Street Research, had previously alleged similar inflated user metrics against Yalla in May 2021.
body: Yalla Group is an audio-based social network listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker YALA. The company operates voice and live-room products in Gulf markets and the Middle East.

On June 2, 2025, short seller Pelican Way Research published a 49-slide presentation on the company. Pelican Way compared Yalla's reported revenue metrics and downloads against third-party sources and its own calculations.
The presentation alleged that Yalla's reported figures sharply contrasted with those sources. Pelican Way also alleged that the company's app reviews showed signs of extreme artificial activity.
Two other firms, Akram's Razor and Swan Street Research, had previously alleged similar inflated user metrics against Yalla in May 2021.

title: A factory supplying Samsung received recruiting help from Xinjiang in 2023
points: The New York Times reported that Transimage had received help recruiting workers from a labor dispatch center in Akqi County, Xinjiang, in 2023.
Their investigation found that these programs were much more extensive than previously known.
The latest dated finding concerned the May 29, 2025 investigation by The New York Times and its reporting partners.
body: Jiangsu Chuanyi Technology Company Ltd., also known as Transimage, is a Chinese company linked to Samsung's supply chain. The available reporting did not describe what the company told investors about its workforce or recruitment practices.
On May 29, 2025, The New York Times reported that Transimage had received help recruiting workers from a labor dispatch center in Akqi County, Xinjiang, in 2023.

The New York Times, the Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Der Spiegel jointly investigated state-led programs that moved Uyghur workers from Xinjiang to factories across China. Their investigation found that these programs were much more extensive than previously known. Transimage was among the companies named in the reporting.

The investigation raised questions about forced labor in supply chains serving global brands. Samsung said it had found no evidence of forced labor at Jiangsu Chuanyi Technology. Samsung also said it prohibited suppliers from using any form of forced labor.

The latest dated finding concerned the May 29, 2025 investigation by The New York Times and its reporting partners. It documented recruiting assistance involving a Xinjiang labor dispatch center in 2023, while Samsung disputed the implication that forced labor had occurred at the company.

title: TMC projected a $6.8 billion value. Its smelter's website listed a 57% higher fee.
points: BMF Reports said independent footage and industry sources showed 14 verifiable days of uninterrupted offshore testing for the vessel Hidden Gem, compared with TMC's claim of 90 days.
Iceberg Research checked supplier Pacific Metals' website and found a planned processing charge of $120 per wet tonne, 57% above TMC's $76 assumption.
TMC released its pre-feasibility study reporting a mineral reserve of 51 million wet tonnes.
body: TMC the metals company Inc. is a deep-sea mining company listed on Nasdaq. It told investors it would lift polymetallic nodules from the ocean floor using existing partner assets and projected a net present value of $6.8 billion.

On May 27, 2025, short sellers BMF Reports and Iceberg Research published separate reports on the company. BMF Reports said independent footage and industry sources showed 14 verifiable days of uninterrupted offshore testing for the vessel Hidden Gem, compared with TMC's claim of 90 days.

Iceberg Research checked supplier Pacific Metals' website and found a planned processing charge of $120 per wet tonne, 57% above TMC's $76 assumption. Adjusting TMC's inputs, Iceberg Research estimated a negative $721 million net present value.

On August 4, 2025, TMC released its pre-feasibility study reporting a mineral reserve of 51 million wet tonnes. On August 18, 2025, Iceberg Research said company employees had written key sections and noted that TMC had no binding commercial agreements with partners Allseas and Pacific Metals.

title: Karnataka Bank executives spent past their limits. The board refused to approve it.
points: Independent analyst Hemindra Hazari reviewed the notes in the bank's fourth-quarter financial results and questioned the company.
In response to Hazari's query, the bank acknowledged that the unratified appointee had resigned.
Karnataka Bank informed stock exchanges that both executives had resigned, citing personal reasons, and the shares fell 6%.
body: Karnataka Bank Limited is a century-old regional private sector bank in India that had hired outside leadership. Chief executive Srikrishnan Hari Hara Sarma and executive director Sekhar Rao had joined the bank in 2023.

On May 23, 2025, independent analyst Hemindra Hazari reviewed the notes in the bank's fourth-quarter financial results and questioned the company. He reported that the two executives spent money beyond their designated powers and made an unapproved appointment.
The bank's board refused to ratify the expenses and demanded reimbursement from the executives. In response to Hazari's query, the bank acknowledged that the unratified appointee had resigned.

On June 29, 2025, Karnataka Bank informed stock exchanges that both executives had resigned, citing personal reasons, and the shares fell 6%. On September 22, 2026, Hazari reported that the Reserve Bank of India denied variable pay to the former executives over governance concerns.
