title: Aurora pitched a $200 billion market. Short sellers valued it at $10 billion.
points: Short seller Bleecker Street Research published a report saying it held a short position in Aurora, earning when the shares fell.
It said a senior executive at partner Volvo put mass production closer to 2030 and estimated Aurora would need $2-3 billion rather than the ~$750 million it claimed.

Based on talks with employees at partners Volvo and PACCAR, Kerrisdale alleged autonomous trucks would cost about 50% more than manned ones and estimated the viable market at about 17 billion miles, or $8.5 billion to $10 billion.
body: Aurora Innovation is a US autonomous trucking company that told investors it could address a 200 billion mile market. Management projected it could charge $0.65-0.85 per mile and deploy more than 10,000 revenue-generating trucks by the end of 2027.

On May 14, 2025, short seller Bleecker Street Research published a report saying it held a short position in Aurora, earning when the shares fell. It said a senior executive at partner Volvo put mass production closer to 2030 and estimated Aurora would need $2-3 billion rather than the ~$750 million it claimed.

On August 19, 2025, Kerrisdale Capital published a report, also disclosing a short position. Based on talks with employees at partners Volvo and PACCAR, Kerrisdale alleged autonomous trucks would cost about 50% more than manned ones and estimated the viable market at about 17 billion miles, or $8.5 billion to $10 billion.

Bleecker Street Research also reported that co-founder Sterling Anderson had left as Chief Product Officer and Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi left the board in January, while Uber announced $1.0 billion of 2028 notes exchangeable into Aurora shares.

title: Mercurity was valued at $399 million. Its revenue was nearly zero, a short seller said.
points: The short seller said Mercurity traded at 383 times enterprise value to sales.
Morpheus said Mercurity's CEO and CFO had been arrested in China in 2022 and its digital assets seized.
It cited an August 2022 special committee recommendation to suspend Yang Jie after an earlier Hindenburg report.
body: Mercurity Fintech Holding is a New York-based company focused on cryptocurrency mining, AI infrastructure and financial services. Its shares traded near four-year highs following company announcements. Morpheus Research said the business generated virtually no revenue despite its $399 million market value.

On May 8, 2025, Morpheus Research published a report alleging that Mercurity had spent a decade pursuing failed business initiatives and was now promoting AI hardware, fintech and blockchain. The short seller said Mercurity traded at 383 times enterprise value to sales. Morpheus disclosed a short position, meaning it earned when the shares fell.

Morpheus said Mercurity's CEO and CFO had been arrested in China in 2022 and its digital assets seized. It cited an August 2022 special committee recommendation to suspend Yang Jie after an earlier Hindenburg report. Morpheus also visited a purported address of Yingke Precision and reported finding no references on that floor to Yingke Precision, Mercurity, Aifinity or ZJK.
On June 20, 2025, US~Observer reported it was investigating Morpheus Research's own short-selling tactics, including questions about its funding, trading and report validity.

title: Klaviyo reported $370.6 million in quarterly revenue while short seller claims went unsupported.
points: None of the available records contain the text of the report, any evidence gathered by the short seller, or any trading position.
Records from 2026 show no confirmation of a corporate failure or accounting error.
Instead, Klaviyo launched native landing pages in February 2026 and released an AI campaign builder called Composer in public beta on June 30, 2026.
body: Klaviyo is a publicly traded retention-marketing platform used by e-commerce merchants, particularly on Shopify, to send emails and track sales. The company went public in 2023 and reported having over 205,000 customers.

On May 5, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log published a report on Klaviyo. None of the available records contain the text of the report, any evidence gathered by the short seller, or any trading position.

Records from 2026 show no confirmation of a corporate failure or accounting error. Instead, Klaviyo launched native landing pages in February 2026 and released an AI campaign builder called Composer in public beta on June 30, 2026.

On August 16, 2026, Klaviyo reported second-quarter revenue of $370.6 million, up 26%, and raised its full-year guidance to a range of $1.526 billion to $1.534 billion. The short seller's allegations were not borne out in these records.

title: Short sellers targeted Nexstar Media Group. Its shares later rose 43.28%.
points: Two days later, on May 2, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published its own report alleging that Nexstar was masking a decline through acquisitions, outdated technology, and financial engineering.
BMF Reports alleged that Nexstar insiders sold over $48 million in shares over six months while the company continued aggressive share buybacks to support metrics and investor sentiment.
At the time BMF Reports wrote its report, Nexstar shares traded at $149.42.
body: Nexstar Media Group, Inc. is listed on Nasdaq and is the largest local television broadcaster in the United States. The company owns or provides services to over 200 stations in nearly 120 markets, along with 138 websites and 229 apps, and presents itself as a modern, digitally scaled media business.

On April 30, 2025, Grizzly Research published a report saying Nexstar was failing with its digital strategy. Two days later, on May 2, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published its own report alleging that Nexstar was masking a decline through acquisitions, outdated technology, and financial engineering.

BMF Reports alleged that Nexstar insiders sold over $48 million in shares over six months while the company continued aggressive share buybacks to support metrics and investor sentiment. At the time BMF Reports wrote its report, Nexstar shares traded at $149.42.

title: LinkedIn banned health data on its Insight Tag. State insurance sites sent it anyway.
points: In April and May 2025, The Markup and CalMatters audited all 19 state-run health exchange websites and found four more states sending data.
Covered California confirmed the data sharing began in February 2024, removed the trackers, and began a review, while Nevada and Massachusetts stopped sending data to LinkedIn.
House lawmakers demanded answers from Covered California by July 1.
body: LinkedIn is a technology company whose Insight Tag tool helps clients target advertising. LinkedIn's policies prohibited customers from installing the tag on web pages that collect or contain sensitive health-related data.

On April 28, 2025, The Markup and CalMatters published forensic tests of California's health exchange website, coveredca.com, conducted in February and March. The reporters found more than 60 trackers on the site and reported that the Insight Tag sent LinkedIn visitors' answers on whether they were pregnant, blind, transgender, used many prescription drugs, or had experienced domestic abuse.

In April and May 2025, The Markup and CalMatters audited all 19 state-run health exchange websites and found four more states sending data. They reported that Nevada Health Link sent LinkedIn whether visitors took Fluoxetine, and Massachusetts Health Connector sent whether visitors were pregnant, blind, or disabled.

LinkedIn cited its policy prohibiting the tag on health pages and later declined to comment. Covered California confirmed the data sharing began in February 2024, removed the trackers, and began a review, while Nevada and Massachusetts stopped sending data to LinkedIn.

On May 2, 2025, a proposed class-action lawsuit in the Northern District of California accused LinkedIn and Google of intercepting health data without user consent. On June 23, 2025, House lawmakers demanded answers from Covered California by July 1.

title: Backblaze capitalized 9.8% to 14.4% of revenue in software costs each year
points: The firm reviewed financial statements and compared Backblaze against 42 software peers.
Morpheus Research alleged that Backblaze capitalized software development costs equal to 9.8% to 14.4% of revenue each year since 2022, nearly five times the peer average.
Backblaze denied all the allegations and said Morpheus Research was trying to manipulate its stock price for financial gain.
body: Backblaze is a California cloud storage and backup provider listed on Nasdaq. In Q3 2024, it told investors it would reach positive adjusted free cash flow by Q4 2025.

On April 24, 2025, Morpheus Research published a report on Backblaze and said it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. The firm reviewed financial statements and compared Backblaze against 42 software peers.

Morpheus Research alleged that Backblaze capitalized software development costs equal to 9.8% to 14.4% of revenue each year since 2022, nearly five times the peer average. Drawing on October 2024 lawsuits from two former senior employees, the report also alleged that the CFO sent inflated cash flow forecasts to auditors in 2023 and that founders sold 10,000 shares a day after the April 2022 lock-up expired.
On April 29, 2025, Backblaze denied all the allegations and said Morpheus Research was trying to manipulate its stock price for financial gain.

title: BioAge Labs dropped over 76% after halting an obesity drug trial
points: Following the trial halt, shares of BioAge Labs fell by over 76%, and the stock experienced an 80% dip.
Investors treated the company as having little else to offer.
Although the case header labels Ragnarok Research a short seller, the report said the firm held a long position and viewed the drop as an overreaction.
body: BioAge Labs is a biotechnology company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker BIOA. In December 2024, the company abruptly halted its STRIDES Phase 2 clinical trial for its experimental obesity drug candidate, Azelaprag.
Following the trial halt, shares of BioAge Labs fell by over 76%, and the stock experienced an 80% dip. Investors treated the company as having little else to offer.

On April 14, 2025, Ragnarok Research published a report stating that it had bought shares of BioAge Labs. Although the case header labels Ragnarok Research a short seller, the report said the firm held a long position and viewed the drop as an overreaction.
Ragnarok Research stated that BioAge Labs held cash reserves more than double its market capitalization, along with an undervalued asset that could support future growth.

title: NIO's ONVO deliveries fell 51.7%, pulling the stock to a six-year low
points: In October, NIO delivered 34,246 cars, down 15.2% from the previous year.
Deliveries for ONVO, its family brand, dropped 51.7% to 8,383 vehicles and accounted for all of the decline, while the NIO brand grew 5.7%.
NIO scheduled its next earnings report for December 1, 2026.
body: NIO Inc. is a Cayman Islands holding company with American depositary shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It has no equity ownership in its consolidated variable interest entities in China, including Beijing NIO Network Technology Co., Ltd. The company told investors its fourth-quarter goal was more than 40,000 vehicle deliveries a month.

In October, NIO delivered 34,246 cars, down 15.2% from the previous year. Deliveries for ONVO, its family brand, dropped 51.7% to 8,383 vehicles and accounted for all of the decline, while the NIO brand grew 5.7%.

To meet its fourth-quarter target, NIO needed about 42,900 deliveries in each of November and December. Earlier, in its second-quarter 2026 earnings report, the company posted revenue of $32.14 billion and adjusted earnings per share of -$0.29, and shares fell 4.37% to $4.045.
By November 19, 2026, NIO shares had fallen 15% in a week and touched a six-year low. NIO scheduled its next earnings report for December 1, 2026.

title: A short seller questioned Monster's accounting after a 2023 auditor change
points: The report alleged that consumers were shifting toward healthier energy and hydration drinks, slowing Monster's growth in the US and Canada.
Spruce Point also alleged concerns with Monster's financial reporting and accounting choices after the company changed auditors in 2023.
The company said the report contained false and misleading characterizations from non-credible sources and stated it would not comment further.
body: Monster Beverage Corporation is a holding company based in Corona, California, and listed on Nasdaq. Through its subsidiaries, it markets and distributes energy drinks and alcoholic beverages.

On April 8, 2025, short-selling firm Spruce Point Capital Management published a report and issued a strong sell opinion on Monster following a forensic financial review. The report alleged that consumers were shifting toward healthier energy and hydration drinks, slowing Monster's growth in the US and Canada.

Spruce Point also alleged concerns with Monster's financial reporting and accounting choices after the company changed auditors in 2023. The report further claimed Monster had failed to separate the duties of its chief financial officer, chief accounting officer, and chief operating officer roles, and faced unsustainable international growth.

On April 9, 2025, Monster issued a statement denying the claims. The company said the report contained false and misleading characterizations from non-credible sources and stated it would not comment further.

title: KULR projected up to $350 million in annual revenue. It missed past forecasts by 50%.
points: The firm alleged that KULR missed all past projections by at least 50% and recognized the full $1,800,000 value of a five-year licensing deal in 2024 after signing it two days before year-end.
Grizzly Research alleged that without booking that full $1,800,000 contract upfront, fourth-quarter 2024 revenue would have been $1.71 million instead of a record quarter.
Short seller RedFlag Research published a separate report on KULR examining its Bitcoin exposure, promotional activity, and fundamental gaps.
body: KULR Technology Group, Inc. is a San Diego-based company that develops thermal management and energy storage systems for batteries and electronics. In early 2022, CEO Michael Mo told investors that new initiatives had a top-line revenue potential of $250 million to $350 million, up from about $2.4 million in 2021.

On April 3, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report reviewing KULR's filings, contract records, and earnings calls. The firm alleged that KULR missed all past projections by at least 50% and recognized the full $1,800,000 value of a five-year licensing deal in 2024 after signing it two days before year-end.

Grizzly Research alleged that without booking that full $1,800,000 contract upfront, fourth-quarter 2024 revenue would have been $1.71 million instead of a record quarter. Shares of KULR fell on April 3, 2025.
On January 12, 2026, short seller RedFlag Research published a separate report on KULR examining its Bitcoin exposure, promotional activity, and fundamental gaps.

title: Tesla booked 26 billion euros in Dutch turnover but paid almost no Dutch tax
points: Follow the Money published an analysis of Tesla's annual accounts in the United States, Germany, and the Netherlands and interviewed tax specialists.
It reported that Tesla Motors Netherlands recorded about 26 billion euros in turnover in 2023, nearly a third of Tesla Inc.'s revenue of some $97 billion.
Follow the Money reported that Tesla had reshuffled its corporate structure again and that Singapore was on the Dutch Parliament's radar.
body: Tesla is an American maker of electric vehicles and energy storage systems with its European headquarters in Amsterdam.

On April 12, 2025, Follow the Money published an analysis of Tesla's annual accounts in the United States, Germany, and the Netherlands and interviewed tax specialists. It reported that Tesla Motors Netherlands recorded about 26 billion euros in turnover in 2023, nearly a third of Tesla Inc.'s revenue of some $97 billion.

The report said the Dutch entity contracted car production to its German sister company in Brandenburg while paying very little corporate income tax in either country. After Dutch anti-abuse rules took effect in 2020, Tesla inserted a Singaporean entity between its Dutch headquarters and its US parent, channelling about $18 billion in untaxed profits through the Netherlands and Singapore.

Tesla did not respond to requests for comment. On July 13, 2026, Follow the Money reported that Tesla had reshuffled its corporate structure again and that Singapore was on the Dutch Parliament's radar.

title: Doximity claimed 80% of US doctors. Investigators said it scraped a database.
points: Marketing staff from top pharmaceutical firms also described contract delivery patterns, impression throttling, and gaps between claimed and actual engagement.
Doximity shares traded below their 2021 initial public offering price of $26.
Doximity raised its full-year revenue guidance to $678 million to $683 million and reported $713 million in liquidity.
body: Doximity is a publicly traded online network for healthcare professionals that makes money by letting pharmaceutical companies target doctors with ads. It told investors it reached over 80% of U.S. physicians.

On March 30, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log highlighted research by independent analyst Lauren Balik on Doximity. Balik alleged that Doximity scraped the NPI database to pre-populate profiles for every U.S. physician, pressured doctors into claiming them, and pulled forward revenue on large accounts as smaller customers churned.

In December 2025, physician writer kianimd published an analysis building on Balik and Jehoshaphat Research, noting Doximity faced a securities lawsuit over the allegedly misleading active-member metric. Marketing staff from top pharmaceutical firms also described contract delivery patterns, impression throttling, and gaps between claimed and actual engagement.

By August 18, 2026, Doximity shares traded below their 2021 initial public offering price of $26. On November 11, 2026, Doximity raised its full-year revenue guidance to $678 million to $683 million and reported $713 million in liquidity.

title: ODDITY Tech claimed to be online-only while operating 43 stores
points: The firm said a three-month on-the-ground investigation used dozens of interviews and thousands of documents to check the company.
NINGI Research alleged that ODDITY Tech owned and operated 43 brick-and-mortar retail stores through a subsidiary called Il Makiage Beauty rather than running an online-only business.
The report also alleged that insiders and backers sold over $400 million of stock at the IPO and said the company relied on dishonest marketing tactics and hundreds of undisclosed lawsuits.
body: ODDITY Tech Ltd. is an Israeli beauty and wellness company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker ODD. It launched its Il Makiage cosmetics brand in 2013 and its SpoiledChild skincare brand in 2022. The company told investors it ran a 100 percent digital business model.

On May 21, 2024, short seller NINGI Research published a report on ODDITY Tech and said it was short the stock. The firm said a three-month on-the-ground investigation used dozens of interviews and thousands of documents to check the company.

NINGI Research alleged that ODDITY Tech owned and operated 43 brick-and-mortar retail stores through a subsidiary called Il Makiage Beauty rather than running an online-only business. The report also alleged that insiders and backers sold over $400 million of stock at the IPO and said the company relied on dishonest marketing tactics and hundreds of undisclosed lawsuits.
Both NINGI Research and The Nexus Files had published reports challenging ODDITY Tech's growth narrative and valuation.

title: Gotham City said Kyndryl overstated adjusted EBITDA by 61% to 72%
points: The firm interviewed an industry consultant and reviewed Kyndryl's accounting since 2023, when Kyndryl stopped reporting its costs to IBM.
It calculated that adjusted EBITDA was 61% to 72% lower if costs were capitalized in line with peers, and warned of higher IBM costs.
Kyndryl shares fell nearly 13% on March 27, 2025.
body: Kyndryl is an IT services and consulting provider spun off from IBM. It told investors that growth in consulting would offset declines in legacy mainframe services.

On March 27, 2025, short seller Gotham City Research published a report on the company, earning when the shares fall. The firm interviewed an industry consultant and reviewed Kyndryl's accounting since 2023, when Kyndryl stopped reporting its costs to IBM.

Gotham City alleged that Kyndryl shifted managed service accounts into consulting to create an illusion of growth and manipulated adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow. It calculated that adjusted EBITDA was 61% to 72% lower if costs were capitalized in line with peers, and warned of higher IBM costs.
Kyndryl shares fell nearly 13% on March 27, 2025. A Kyndryl spokesperson rejected the report's conclusions as inaccurate and designed to manipulate the stock for the short seller's benefit.
On March 28, 2025, Gotham City published a follow-up report stating that Kyndryl was trying to mislead people.

title: Vita Coco faced a $90 million revenue threat from one Costco contract
points: BMF examined retail sales data and estimated that the contract represented up to $90 million in annual revenue, nearly 25% of Vita Coco's 2023 total.
NINGI predicted a $90 million revenue shortfall by the end of 2025.
BMF alleged that Costco had already dropped Vita Coco in 2024 and that the company had not disclosed the loss.
body: The Vita Coco Company sells coconut water and other drinks in the United States. It presented itself to investors as a growing beverage business with a strong supply chain and expanding product lines. Its private-label operation also produced coconut water for retailers, including Costco.

On March 26, 2025, short sellers NINGI Research and BMF Reports published separate reports alleging that Vita Coco was losing its Costco business. NINGI examined import records and said Costco was moving Kirkland coconut water production to a competitor. BMF examined retail sales data and estimated that the contract represented up to $90 million in annual revenue, nearly 25% of Vita Coco's 2023 total.

NINGI predicted a $90 million revenue shortfall by the end of 2025. BMF alleged that Costco had already dropped Vita Coco in 2024 and that the company had not disclosed the loss. NINGI also alleged undisclosed related-party transactions and inventory shortages. NINGI held a short position, which would benefit if Vita Coco's shares fell.

On March 27, NINGI published a follow-up criticizing Vita Coco's rebuttal. It reported that supplier Ducoco, responsible for 8.5% of Vita Coco's supply, had sought bankruptcy protection in February 2025 with $118 million in debt. NINGI said Vita Coco had not addressed that bankruptcy on its earnings calls.

title: Tracking devices followed UK waste tyres to India's second-biggest importer
points: The investigators said they used data from tracking devices planted in containers of used tyres to follow the shipments.
The report said trackers placed in two tyre bales bought by Nine Corporation arrived at Mundra port in northeast India the previous year.
Farmers in Wada showed SourceMaterial and the BBC young mangoes covered with soot and dropping dead from the trees.
body: Nine Corporation is India's second-biggest tyre importer and is owned by Group CNJ. Its founder, Chetan Joshi, chairs the All India Rubber and Tyre Recyclers Association, which represents the sector to the Indian government.

On March 25, 2025, SourceMaterial and the BBC published an investigation into the trade of used tyres from the UK to India. The investigators said they used data from tracking devices planted in containers of used tyres to follow the shipments.

The report said trackers placed in two tyre bales bought by Nine Corporation arrived at Mundra port in northeast India the previous year. SourceMaterial and the BBC reported that brokers openly advertised imported UK tyres for pyrolysis on Facebook groups, though the report noted that companies like Nine Corporation and CNJ do not always operate pyrolysis themselves.
Farmers in Wada showed SourceMaterial and the BBC young mangoes covered with soot and dropping dead from the trees. Neither Group CNJ nor Chetan Joshi responded to requests for comment.

title: Trackers followed UK tyres to a pyrolysis plant that blew up in India
points: SourceMaterial and BBC File on 4 Investigates published a joint investigation into the trade.
An Environment Agency official wrote in an email seen by SourceMaterial that monitoring a site outside its jurisdiction was not within its powers.
MD Pyrolysis did not respond to requests for comment.
body: MD Pyrolysis ran one of seven pyrolysis plants in the village of Wada in India. The plants process used tyres, including waste tyres imported from the UK.

On March 25, 2025, SourceMaterial and BBC File on 4 Investigates published a joint investigation into the trade. They used data from tracking devices planted in containers of used tyres to follow shipments from the UK to India, and found brokers advertising imported UK tyres for pyrolysis on Facebook groups.

An Environment Agency official wrote in an email seen by SourceMaterial that monitoring a site outside its jurisdiction was not within its powers. Scientists at Imperial College London told the investigators that workers exposed to pyrolysis pollution face risks of respiratory, cardiovascular and neurological diseases and certain cancers, while Wada farmers showed young mangoes covered with soot and dropping dead from trees.

After an explosion at the MD Pyrolysis plant in Wada, resident Kalpesh Patil used freedom of information laws the next day to ask officials for copies of the permits for the village's seven plants. MD Pyrolysis did not respond to requests for comment.

title: Ibotta promised cashback on everyday items. Users said they could not withdraw it.
points: The Bear Cave said it makes money only from reader subscriptions and never bets against the companies it writes about.
The report also noted slowing revenue growth, falling from 43% in the first quarter of 2024 to negative 1% in the fourth quarter.
Ibotta's stock was down about 67% since its April 2024 initial public offering, and founder Bryan Leach remained chief executive officer.
body: Ibotta is a digital coupon company listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It told investors it brings cashback coupons for everyday items into the loyalty programs of major retailers through an AI-enabled platform.

On March 20, 2025, The Bear Cave published a report calling Ibotta a broken business. The Bear Cave said it makes money only from reader subscriptions and never bets against the companies it writes about.

The Bear Cave reviewed online commentary and complaints submitted to the Better Business Bureau. It said users found it easy to earn virtual cashback in the app, but difficult to withdraw the money into bank accounts. The report also noted slowing revenue growth, falling from 43% in the first quarter of 2024 to negative 1% in the fourth quarter.
An Ibotta representative declined to comment on the report that day.
By April 12, 2026, Ibotta's stock was down about 67% since its April 2024 initial public offering, and founder Bryan Leach remained chief executive officer.

title: Hesai told US courts it had no military ties. Short sellers pointed to state TV.
points: Hesai shares came under pressure that day.
Hesai issued a statement in response saying it was aware of the Blue Orca Capital report.

Short seller BMF Reports published its own report when Hesai shares traded at $22.30, saying a former Hesai employee confirmed witnessing production for military applications at the company's Shanghai facilities.
body: Hesai Group is a Nasdaq-listed maker of three-dimensional light detection and ranging (lidar) sensors with offices in Shanghai, Palo Alto and Stuttgart. In January 2024, the U.S. Department of Defense placed Hesai on a list of Chinese military companies, and Hesai sued to be removed from it.

On March 18, 2025, short seller Blue Orca Capital published a report and said it was short the stock, meaning it earns when the shares fall. Blue Orca alleged that Hesai lied to investors, U.S. authorities and the court about military use of its lidar technology, citing images from Chinese state-owned CCTV that appeared to show a Chinese military vehicle with a Hesai lidar system.
Hesai shares came under pressure that day. On March 19, 2025, Hesai issued a statement in response saying it was aware of the Blue Orca Capital report.

On March 24, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published its own report when Hesai shares traded at $22.30, saying a former Hesai employee confirmed witnessing production for military applications at the company's Shanghai facilities.

title: Appian sold compliance software while its key European client stayed in Russia
points: The report cited a February Bloomberg article stating Russia held €4.4 billion of Raiffeisen Bank's profits and that the bank financed Russian military suppliers.
Full-year 2025 revenue reached $726.9 million, up from $617.0 million in 2024, and the company recorded its first full year of GAAP net income.
Appian had also won a US Army agreement worth up to $500 million over ten years.
body: Appian Corporation is a US software company listed on Nasdaq that sells low-code business automation tools to large enterprises and federal agencies.

On March 18, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log published a report alleging that a large share of Appian's European revenue and operations came from Austrian lender Raiffeisen Bank. The report said Raiffeisen Bank built compliance processes on Appian's software through a Kosovo spin-off called Raiffeisen Tech while operating in Russia and facing criticism over anti-money laundering standards.

The report cited a February Bloomberg article stating Russia held €4.4 billion of Raiffeisen Bank's profits and that the bank financed Russian military suppliers. On March 23, 2025, independent researcher Lauren Balik repeated the allegation in The Bear Cave newsletter.

Appian's business later grew rather than collapsed. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $726.9 million, up from $617.0 million in 2024, and the company recorded its first full year of GAAP net income. By July 21, 2026, Appian had also won a US Army agreement worth up to $500 million over ten years.

title: Solaris said its turbine unit was diversified. Its 10-K showed 96% came from xAI.
points: The report said Solaris paid $60 million in cash, about 16.5 million shares, and paid off $71 million in debt for turbines worth $54.7 million.
The report cited the company's 10-K filing showing that 96% of turbine leasing revenue during 2024 came from Elon Musk's xAI.
Shares of Solaris fell 17% on March 17, 2025, following the research note.
body: Solaris Energy Infrastructure is a $1.65 billion Houston-based mobile power and oilfield services company. In July 2024, it announced a plan to buy Mobile Energy Rentals, telling investors the business had a diversified earnings stream and recognized industry leaders.

On March 17, 2025, short-selling firm Morpheus Research published a report on X targeting Solaris. The report said Solaris paid $60 million in cash, about 16.5 million shares, and paid off $71 million in debt for turbines worth $54.7 million.

Morpheus Research alleged that co-owners John Tuma and John Johnson turned those turbines into cash and stock worth about $246 million at closing and closer to $460 million by the report date. The report cited the company's 10-K filing showing that 96% of turbine leasing revenue during 2024 came from Elon Musk's xAI.
Shares of Solaris fell 17% on March 17, 2025, following the research note. That drop was the largest single-day decline for the stock since January.

title: Brokerage commission jumped three-fold at PB Fintech. The CEO called the impact minimal.
points: Trudence Capital alleged that total commission paid to insurance distributors rose sharply after March 2023.
The report stated that PB Fintech's brokerage commission earned jumped three-fold in FY24, which differed from what management told investors on earnings calls.
Separately, in March 2025, founder and chairman Yashish Dahiya won a settlement order from the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
body: PB Fintech is an Indian financial company that runs the lending arm Paisabazaar. On post-earnings calls in Q4FY23 and Q1 FY24, CEO Yashish Dahiya told analysts that commission changes had a minimal impact on revenue and that the take rate had no material shifts.

In March 2025, Mumbai-based forensic research firm Trudence Capital published a report titled 'Premium Promises and Discounted Truths'. The report questioned PB Fintech's past revenue recognition practices and the role of Paisabazaar.

Trudence Capital alleged that total commission paid to insurance distributors rose sharply after March 2023. The report stated that PB Fintech's brokerage commission earned jumped three-fold in FY24, which differed from what management told investors on earnings calls.

Separately, in March 2025, founder and chairman Yashish Dahiya won a settlement order from the Securities and Exchange Board of India. That case involved allegedly suppressing price-sensitive information about an overseas acquisition from the stock exchanges.

title: Unplugged cables at the border. OSI Systems booked $343 million on a $612 million contract.
points: Culper said its investigators visited border crossings in Mexico in February 2024 and checked Google Earth.
At Reynosa, investigators found seven light vehicle systems and two cargo systems blocked off with ropes, caution tape, or barriers, with cables unplugged and loose equipment on the ground.
Soren Aandahl of Blue Orca Capital presented a short pitch on OSI Systems at the Sohn New York Conference.
body: OSI Systems is a United States designer and manufacturer of electronic security, screening, and inspection systems listed on Nasdaq. On January 17, 2023, it announced an award of over $200 million for cargo and vehicle inspection systems, part of a $612 million contract including $424 million in product and installation revenues.

On March 13, 2025, short seller Culper Research published a report on the company and said it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. Culper estimated OSI had recognized $343 million in revenues through the second quarter of 2025, while insiders sold $83.7 million in stock over three years and $40.8 million in the past year.

Culper said its investigators visited border crossings in Mexico in February 2024 and checked Google Earth. At Reynosa, investigators found seven light vehicle systems and two cargo systems blocked off with ropes, caution tape, or barriers, with cables unplugged and loose equipment on the ground.
On May 12, 2026, Soren Aandahl of Blue Orca Capital presented a short pitch on OSI Systems at the Sohn New York Conference. The pitch focused on revenue recognition and cash collection.

title: XP said a short seller's report caused over $100 million in harm and sued
points: XP said it suffered more than $100 million in harm to its business and reputation, with longtime clients, investors, and business partners withdrawing funds.
XP also asked authorities to investigate criminal claims against Grizzly CEO Siegfried Eggert in Brazil.
Grizzly Research issued a public statement standing behind its report and its accuracy.
body: XP Inc. is a Brazilian financial services company centered on investment management, advisory, and digital financial services. It is listed on Nasdaq.

On March 12, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report titled "XP's (Nasdaq: XP) Entire Profits Are Dependent on What Insiders Call a 'Madoff-Like Ponzi Scheme'." Grizzly Research said its report was based on generally available information, field research, inferences, and deductions.

On July 7, 2025, XP filed a defamation lawsuit against Grizzly Research in federal court in Manhattan. XP said it suffered more than $100 million in harm to its business and reputation, with longtime clients, investors, and business partners withdrawing funds. XP also asked authorities to investigate criminal claims against Grizzly CEO Siegfried Eggert in Brazil.

On November 21, 2025, Grizzly Research issued a public statement standing behind its report and its accuracy. It stated that its affiliates held a short position in XP Inc., meaning they earn when the shares fall.

title: Gorilla's AI hardware was allegedly rebranded PCs. Shares fell 4.95%.
points: The Bear Cave questioned the business after identifying that approximately 94% of revenue came from two customers: Egypt's government and Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau.
Citron Research followed with allegations concerning litigation involving one of Gorilla's announced partners.
A July 6, 2026 EAA Partners report revisited the company's shift toward AI infrastructure and questioned whether its business supported its claims.
body: Gorilla Technology Group is a UK-based technology company that describes itself as a provider of security, network and business intelligence systems. Its shares had risen about 1,200% over six months, driven largely by investor interest in announced deals and partnerships.

On March 6, 2025, The Bear Cave questioned the business after identifying that approximately 94% of revenue came from two customers: Egypt's government and Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau. Citron Research followed with allegations concerning litigation involving one of Gorilla's announced partners.

On April 4, 2025, Culper Research published a report alleging fabricated contracts, misleading products and questionable commercial partners. Its investigators examined product listings, visited a partner's location and checked geographic information. Culper alleged that Gorilla's proprietary AI hardware consisted of rebranded commercially available computers and cameras, and questioned its multi-billion-dollar pipeline. Culper held a short position, which benefited if the shares fell.
Gorilla shares fell 4.95% on April 4. The company rejected the accusations as false and misleading, and said the reports had damaged its reputation and depressed its share price.

On April 16, 2025, Gorilla announced that it had filed a defamation lawsuit against Culper Research and founder Christian Lamarco, seeking compensatory and punitive damages. A July 6, 2026 EAA Partners report revisited the company's shift toward AI infrastructure and questioned whether its business supported its claims.

title: Short sellers alleged Globe Life wrote policies for dead people
points: Viceroy Research published an analysis of Globe Life's 2024 10-K report.
Viceroy said its operations faced increasing headwinds from regulatory scrutiny and reputational problems.
Following the March 26, 2025 BMF Reports release, Globe Life shares rose 17.64%.
body: Globe Life is a US insurance provider that offers life and supplemental health insurance to middle-income families. The company positioned itself as a dependable insurer with a large agent force.

On March 3, 2025, Viceroy Research published an analysis of Globe Life's 2024 10-K report. Viceroy said its operations faced increasing headwinds from regulatory scrutiny and reputational problems. The firm noted it stood to gain if the stock price declined.

On March 26, 2025, short seller BMF Reports released an investigation alleging systemic fraud inside Globe Life. The report accused the insurer of forging customer signatures and issuing policies in the names of dead or fictitious people to inflate policy counts and revenue.
Following the March 26, 2025 BMF Reports release, Globe Life shares rose 17.64%.

title: Rumble spent over $125 million on creators against $81 million in revenue
points: The report said Rumble spent over $125 million on programming and content in 2023, against $81 million in revenue.
Pelican Way argued Rumble was worth less than $5 per share, about half its then-current price.
It cited a $3.0 billion market cap as of February 28, 2025, versus a $1.47 billion streaming valuation.
body: Rumble Inc. is a US video-sharing platform founded by Chris Pavlovski as an alternative to YouTube. It promoted user growth and new monetization products, and in December 2024 Tether made a $775 million strategic investment in the company.

In March 2025, Pelican Way Research published a short report questioning Rumble's valuation and operations. Pelican Way held a short position, so it earned if the shares fell. It reviewed SEC filings, earnings calls and creator spending.

The report said Rumble spent over $125 million on programming and content in 2023, against $81 million in revenue. It alleged that monthly active users had declined despite management claims, and questioned Rumble's new monetization products.

Pelican Way argued Rumble was worth less than $5 per share, about half its then-current price. It cited a $3.0 billion market cap as of February 28, 2025, versus a $1.47 billion streaming valuation. These were valuation estimates, not cash losses.
Rumble's net loss had widened to $80.3 million from $30.2 million the prior year.

title: A $35 billion AI server maker re-hired executives from a 2018 accounting issue
points: The report also alleged that Super Micro Computer re-hired top executives who were directly involved in a previous accounting issue that led to a temporary Nasdaq delisting in 2018.
By the time of the news report, the stock had fallen 55% from its March all-time high to $547.64.
Those indicted included a Super Micro Computer board member named in the Hindenburg report and another company manager.
body: Super Micro Computer is a US technology company that makes artificial intelligence servers. A partnership with Nvidia helped it capitalize on surging demand for those servers, lifting its market value to $35 billion.

In August 2024, Hindenburg Research published a report on the company and stated it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. Hindenburg said it found evidence of accounting manipulation, undisclosed related party transactions, and sanction and export control failures in China and Russia.

The report also alleged that Super Micro Computer re-hired top executives who were directly involved in a previous accounting issue that led to a temporary Nasdaq delisting in 2018. By the time of the news report, the stock had fallen 55% from its March all-time high to $547.64.

In March 2026, the Department of Justice criminally indicted three individuals over export control failures. Those indicted included a Super Micro Computer board member named in the Hindenburg report and another company manager.

title: Prosecutors suspected Enraf-Nonius of paying bribes for Sri Lanka hospitals
points: The report identified Enraf-Nonius as the central figure in the investigation.
According to the report, the government of Sri Lanka had awarded the hospital construction contracts to the Rotterdam company.
The Dutch state insurer is considering filing a claim against Enraf-Nonius.
body: Enraf-Nonius is a Rotterdam-based medical equipment trader led by director Len de Jong. The company exports equipment for physiotherapists and builds hospitals and rehabilitation centers in emerging markets.

In March 2025, Het Financieele Dagblad reported that the Dutch Public Prosecution Service suspected two companies of paying bribes for hospital construction projects in Sri Lanka. The report identified Enraf-Nonius as the central figure in the investigation.
According to the report, the government of Sri Lanka had awarded the hospital construction contracts to the Rotterdam company.
The Dutch state insurer is considering filing a claim against Enraf-Nonius.

title: Rocket Lab targeted a mid-2025 launch. Its shares fell over 10% after a warning.
points: The firm reviewed documents and conducted 23 interviews with industry experts, including former Rocket Lab engineers and executives.
Rocket Lab had $504 million in cash as of September, according to the report.
Rocket Lab shares fell over 10% during trading on February 25.
body: Rocket Lab is a US rocket developer that planned to launch Neutron, a medium-lift rocket designed to compete with SpaceX's Falcon 9. The company repeatedly told investors it expected Neutron to fly by mid-2025. Its shares had risen 485% over the previous year, giving it an $11.2 billion valuation.

On February 25, 2025, Bleecker Street Research alleged that Rocket Lab had misled investors about that schedule. The firm reviewed documents and conducted 23 interviews with industry experts, including former Rocket Lab engineers and executives. It said engine development, production, launch pad construction and rocket transport were behind schedule.

Bleecker Street argued that a launch in 2026 or 2027 could delay Rocket Lab's access to US national security launch contracts. Three aerospace executives estimated that completing Neutron and reaching profitability would cost $300-$600 million. Rocket Lab had $504 million in cash as of September, according to the report.

Bleecker Street disclosed that funds it managed held a short position, which would benefit from a falling share price. Rocket Lab shares fell over 10% during trading on February 25. The available reporting did not include a company response.

On February 25, 2025, law firm Block & Leviton announced an investigation into potential securities law violations at Rocket Lab. Its notice cited Bleecker Street's allegations about Neutron's launch schedule and the company's need for additional capital.

title: Cettire reported $12.5m Adj EBITDA with 30% from one-offs
points: The report alleged that 30% of the $12.5m figure came from one-offs: $1.2m in stock-based compensation, $1.6m in FX, and $0.8m in undisclosed other items.
Crash Capital also said Cettire held $23m in cash less working capital and would need a capital injection at its current run rate.
The shares fell 79.55% since the February 26, 2025 report.
body: Cettire Limited operates a digital marketplace specializing in high-end merchandise, distributing these products to customers across Australia and globally.

On February 26, 2025, short seller Crash Capital published a report stating that Cettire managed $12.5m Adj EBITDA, a 3.1% margin for the half. The report alleged that 30% of the $12.5m figure came from one-offs: $1.2m in stock-based compensation, $1.6m in FX, and $0.8m in undisclosed other items.
Crash Capital also said Cettire held $23m in cash less working capital and would need a capital injection at its current run rate. The shares fell 79.55% since the February 26, 2025 report.

On April 3, 2025, short seller Taxloss published a report stating that Cettire's market cap was $265m and that ending the US de minimis exemption would finish its US business. Taxloss wrote that Cettire's negative working capital of about $98m would consume its $101m cash balance if US sales scaled back.

title: Patients paid for licensed therapists. A short seller said they got AI.
points: The firm alleged that patients unknowingly received therapy from artificial intelligence.
Blue Orca wrote that BetterHelp warned on its website that AI therapy dehumanized patients and could harm their mental health.
News outlets reported the short position on February 19 and February 20, 2025.
body: Teladoc Health is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and runs the BetterHelp mental health platform. Patients on BetterHelp pay for therapy from licensed therapists.

On February 19, 2025, Blue Orca Capital published a report on its website and announced a short position in Teladoc, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The firm alleged that patients unknowingly received therapy from artificial intelligence.

Blue Orca wrote that BetterHelp warned on its website that AI therapy dehumanized patients and could harm their mental health. The report alleged that BetterHelp gave therapists perverse incentives to cut corners with AI, and that accounting maneuvers concealed that Teladoc was far less profitable and generated far less cash than investors were led to believe.
News outlets reported the short position on February 19 and February 20, 2025.

title: Corporate Travel forecast $220-$260m. Its auditor later flagged the accounts.
points: The report noted CTD historically issued next-year guidance at second-half results and had missed revised FY24 guidance, citing macro, politics and a UK contract.
Crash Capital also questioned CTD's statement that it made substantive supplier payments in December 2024.
The report also examined how CTD accounted for ~60% operating margins in FY25, and a tracker listed the shares down 78.62% since the initial report.
body: Corporate Travel Management is an Australian company that arranges travel for corporate clients. In February 2025, it issued early FY26 guidance of $220-$260m, above market expectations of $220m, and its shares rose 10% to 16.50 the day before February 19.

On February 19, 2025, Crash Capital published an analysis questioning the forecast, stating neither the author nor the firm held a long or short position. The report noted CTD historically issued next-year guidance at second-half results and had missed revised FY24 guidance, citing macro, politics and a UK contract.
Crash Capital also questioned CTD's statement that it made substantive supplier payments in December 2024. On May 4, 2025, the author wrote that CTD had never posted guidance 1.5 years early.

On September 29, 2025, Crash Capital reported that CTD had been in a trading halt since August after its newly appointed auditor flagged issues in its FY24 accounts requiring restatement. The report also examined how CTD accounted for ~60% operating margins in FY25, and a tracker listed the shares down 78.62% since the initial report.

title: Pagaya traded at $18.30 while two short sellers published reports
points: Iceberg Research published another report on February 18, 2025, questioning whether risk issues were behind the company.
BMF Reports noted that Pagaya shares traded at $18.30 at the time of writing.
BMF Reports published its report title again on August 28, 2026.
body: Nasdaq-listed Pagaya Technologies is a financial technology enterprise founded in 2016. The company underwrites consumer loans sourced through partnerships with fintech lenders and banks.

On February 11, 2025, Iceberg Research published a report alleging that Pagaya was using other people's money to hide losses. Iceberg Research published another report on February 18, 2025, questioning whether risk issues were behind the company.
On February 26, 2025, BMF Reports published a report on hidden risks in Pagaya Technologies. BMF Reports noted that Pagaya shares traded at $18.30 at the time of writing.
Iceberg Research covered its short position on May 6, 2025. BMF Reports published its report title again on August 28, 2026.

title: Hims guided to $470 million in sales. Credit card data pointed to slowing core growth.
points: Hims shares jumped more than 10% intraday after an FDA committee vote on peptides, before closing around 3% higher at $32.74.
Cedar Grove closed its short position after first-quarter 2026 earnings and initiated a long position during the second quarter.
An October 7, 2026 article reported that Cedar Grove highlighted Hims in its third-quarter investor letter.
body: Hims & Hers Health is a US telehealth platform that sells curated prescription and non-prescription health products. It guided investors to fourth-quarter sales between $465 million and $470 million, alongside sell-side estimates of $469 million.

On February 18, 2025, Cedar Grove Capital Management published a report reiterating a short position, which profits when shares fall. Citing Bank of America commentary and Second Measure credit card data, it alleged that Hims' reliance on GLP-1 treatments exceeded the 26% net sales estimate and that core growth outside GLP-1s had decelerated.

On July 23, 2026, Hims shares jumped more than 10% intraday after an FDA committee vote on peptides, before closing around 3% higher at $32.74. Martin Shkreli publicly disclosed a short position against the move. Cedar Grove closed its short position after first-quarter 2026 earnings and initiated a long position during the second quarter.
On October 6, 2026, Hims closed at $29.47 with a $6.88 billion market capitalization. An October 7, 2026 article reported that Cedar Grove highlighted Hims in its third-quarter investor letter.

title: One photo game accounted for almost all of Zedge's operating losses
points: It estimated that GuruShots accounted for almost 100% of the company's operating losses, while net cash represented about 50% of its market capitalization.
It estimated potential share price upside of 50-250% if Zedge sold the subsidiary, even without a successful turnaround.
The report discussed GuruShots 2.0, a plan to change gameplay and monetization.
body: Zedge, Inc. operated a phone personalization app business and owned GuruShots, a photographic game it acquired in 2022. Its core app generated cash, but the acquired game weighed on the company's results. Management had launched a cost-saving program for the subsidiary.

On January 22, 2025, Ragnarok Research published a bullish investment report on Zedge. It estimated that GuruShots accounted for almost 100% of the company's operating losses, while net cash represented about 50% of its market capitalization. These were the research firm's estimates, not findings by an auditor or regulator.

Ragnarok argued that cutting GuruShots' costs and increasing its revenue could improve Zedge's overall earnings. It estimated potential share price upside of 50-250% if Zedge sold the subsidiary, even without a successful turnaround. That range was a forecast of possible investment returns, not a recorded gain.

On February 7, 2025, Ragnarok published a second bullish report after speaking with Zedge's CEO and GuruShots' product head. The report discussed GuruShots 2.0, a plan to change gameplay and monetization. Ragnarok said those conversations reinforced its confidence in the turnaround.

title: GeneDx's revenue was allegedly inflated by 25% through insurance billing
points: It alleged that GeneDx used code stacking, a billing practice that combined codes to obtain higher insurance payments, and estimated that this inflated revenue by approximately 25%.
Grizzly also pointed to a 2022 dispute with UnitedHealthcare that resulted in a settlement to repay $42 million over four years.
Its reference to over $800 million in fines concerned other perpetrators, not a penalty imposed on GeneDx.
body: GeneDx is a US genetic testing company that specializes in tests for rare genetic disorders. Its shares had risen over 2,500% since the start of 2024, and its stock market value had reached $2 billion, compared with the approximately $330 million paid to acquire the business.

On February 5, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published allegations based on former employee accounts, whistleblower testimony and litigation. It alleged that GeneDx used code stacking, a billing practice that combined codes to obtain higher insurance payments, and estimated that this inflated revenue by approximately 25%.

Grizzly also pointed to a 2022 dispute with UnitedHealthcare that resulted in a settlement to repay $42 million over four years. Former employees alleged that the billing practice continued, while whistleblowers described supposedly independent counseling entities that directed patients exclusively to GeneDx.

The report also described an undisclosed whistleblower action and warned that insurers might seek repayment. Its reference to over $800 million in fines concerned other perpetrators, not a penalty imposed on GeneDx. The supplied accounts gave neither the share price reaction on February 5 nor a company response.

On February 17, 2025, BMF Reports published another article about the alleged billing practices and potential overcharging of Medicare and Medicaid. It repeated the concerns about GeneDx's financial results but provided no subsequent regulatory finding or court decision.

title: Applied Optoelectronics projected $600 million in 800G sales. Short sellers found no samples.
points: Culper conducted more than 20 interviews with former employees, competitors, hyperscalers, and industry experts, and visited company facilities.
The report alleged that Applied Optoelectronics never shipped 800G samples in the third quarter of 2023 and had only planned a September 2024 release.
BMF Reports published a separate report alleging that a former Meta employee confirmed Applied Optoelectronics missed Meta's request window for 800G transceivers.
body: Applied Optoelectronics is a Nasdaq-listed manufacturer of optical transceivers and networking components for data centers and cable television equipment. The company told investors its 800G transceivers were undergoing customer qualifications worth $500 million to $600 million in expected sales, and said it had shipped samples to two customers in the third quarter of 2023.

On February 4, 2025, Culper Research published a report and said it held a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. Culper conducted more than 20 interviews with former employees, competitors, hyperscalers, and industry experts, and visited company facilities. The report alleged that Applied Optoelectronics never shipped 800G samples in the third quarter of 2023 and had only planned a September 2024 release.

Culper also alleged that the company had no disclosed 800G customers, lacked production capacity, and overstated a Microsoft agreement worth over $300 million that carried no minimum purchase obligations. On February 9, 2025, BMF Reports published a separate report alleging that a former Meta employee confirmed Applied Optoelectronics missed Meta's request window for 800G transceivers.
On April 10, 2026, Citron Research called the company's valuation delusional.

title: A 4,000-page rate filing pointed to $2 billion in wildfire claims for Mercury General
points: Wolfpack analyzed a June 2024 rate filing of about 4,000 pages and found Mercury General insured 929 homeowner policies in Altadena, where about 63% of single-family homes were destroyed.
The report alleged gross wildfire losses would exceed $2 billion, exhausting the $1.3 billion reinsurance tower.
Wolfpack published a second report calling Mercury General's earnings release misleading, noting the insurer had already paid out $800 million and excluded FAIR assessments from gross losses.
body: Mercury General is a US insurer. Following the Eaton and Palisades wildfires in Los Angeles, the company told investors it had $1.3 billion in reinsurance and could treat the fires as two separate events to gain an additional $1.2 billion in coverage.

On January 29, 2025, short seller Wolfpack Research published a report and disclosed it held a short position, which profits when shares fall. Wolfpack analyzed a June 2024 rate filing of about 4,000 pages and found Mercury General insured 929 homeowner policies in Altadena, where about 63% of single-family homes were destroyed.

The report alleged gross wildfire losses would exceed $2 billion, exhausting the $1.3 billion reinsurance tower. On February 12, 2025, Wolfpack published a second report calling Mercury General's earnings release misleading, noting the insurer had already paid out $800 million and excluded FAIR assessments from gross losses.

Wolfpack also stated Mercury General was the only carrier among four peers to include subrogation benefits in net loss figures and to estimate an average loss per homeowner policy at 57% of the peer average of $2.4 million.

title: AppLovin claimed nearly 100% incrementality. Short sellers estimated 25% to 35%.
points: On March 27 and March 28, 2025, Muddy Waters Research published reports and said it was short the stock.
Muddy Waters analyzed web traffic and code and alleged that about 52% of AppLovin's e-commerce conversions came from retargeting, with incrementality of only about 25% to 35%.
It also alleged that AppLovin extracted user IDs from Meta, Snap, TikTok, Reddit, and Google to build persistent user identifiers and observed e-commerce client churn of about 23% in Q1.
body: AppLovin is an advertising technology platform for mobile gaming apps and e-commerce. Its chief executive officer, Adam Foroughi, told investors on a Q3 2024 earnings call that clients were experiencing nearly 100% incrementality and claimed almost no client churn.

On February 26, 2025, Culper Research published a report after decompiling app code, interviewing former employees and customers, and sharing research with Fuzzy Panda Research. On March 27 and March 28, 2025, Muddy Waters Research published reports and said it was short the stock.

Muddy Waters analyzed web traffic and code and alleged that about 52% of AppLovin's e-commerce conversions came from retargeting, with incrementality of only about 25% to 35%. It also alleged that AppLovin extracted user IDs from Meta, Snap, TikTok, Reddit, and Google to build persistent user identifiers and observed e-commerce client churn of about 23% in Q1.

On March 31, 2025, Foroughi denied in a blog post that the company created or used persistent identifiers, referencing an analysis by chief technology officer Shikin. On May 7, 2025, Muddy Waters published a follow-up report alleging that those responses contained false statements and that AppLovin continued to use persistent identifiers.

title: Veritas said 40% of Brookfield's distributable earnings lacked cash flow backing
points: In 2025, Veritas Investment Research analysts Dimitry Khmelnitsky and Benjamin Butler examined Brookfield's own disclosures.
It also said Brookfield excluded cash costs and understated sustaining capital expenditures.
Veritas alleged that Brookfield used related-party insurance companies to offload assets at high valuations during challenging markets.
body: Brookfield Corporation is a conglomerate in Canada that pivoted into life insurance through Brookfield Wealth Solutions. Management told investors it aimed to grow its insurance assets from $110 billion to $300 billion by 2029, with the unit accounting for about 75% of expected Distributable Earnings growth through 2030.

In 2025, Veritas Investment Research analysts Dimitry Khmelnitsky and Benjamin Butler examined Brookfield's own disclosures. Veritas estimated that approximately 40% of Brookfield's Distributable Earnings lacked underlying cash flow backing, and were funded instead by return of capital, intercompany equity infusions, and subsidies. It also said Brookfield excluded cash costs and understated sustaining capital expenditures.

Veritas alleged that Brookfield used related-party insurance companies to offload assets at high valuations during challenging markets. On March 6, 2025, the Financial Times published an investigative feature on circular cash flows between Brookfield entities.

Nicholas Goodman, President and CFO of Brookfield Corporation, and Michael McRaith, Vice Chair of Brookfield Wealth Solutions, later presented the company's strategic response and business rationale during a webinar hosted by Veritas.

title: A $1.5 billion AI company relied on an undisclosed partner for revenue
points: According to a later shareholder derivative suit, the short-seller report about an undisclosed related party caused a record stock drop for the company.
A shareholder derivative suit had been filed against iLearningEngines executives, alleging they faked revenue through that undisclosed related party.
The suit also noted that the report had exposed the company to a proposed class action.
body: iLearningEngines Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed education software company that went public through a SPAC. It had reached a peak market valuation of about $1.5 billion.

In August 2024, short seller Hindenburg Research published a report titled "iLearningEngines: An Artificial Intelligence SPAC With Artificial Partners And Artificial Revenue." Hindenburg alleged that the company's partners and revenue were artificial.
According to a later shareholder derivative suit, the short-seller report about an undisclosed related party caused a record stock drop for the company.

By January 21, 2025, a shareholder derivative suit had been filed against iLearningEngines executives, alleging they faked revenue through that undisclosed related party. The suit also noted that the report had exposed the company to a proposed class action.

title: TransMedics shares fell 13% after allegations of organ trafficking and billing fraud
points: The report also alleged unreported device failures and widespread use of devices outside their approved purposes.
Scorpion Capital assigned the shares a target price of $0.
TransMedics shares fell 13% over two trading days following the report.
body: TransMedics is a medical device company that makes Organ Care System devices used in organ transplantation. Its business came under scrutiny after a short seller accused it of billing fraud, unsafe transplant practices and coercive dealings with customers.

On January 10, 2025, Scorpion Capital published a report alleging that TransMedics used kickbacks, fraudulent billing and pressure on customers. The report also alleged unreported device failures and widespread use of devices outside their approved purposes. Scorpion Capital assigned the shares a target price of $0.

TransMedics shares fell 13% over two trading days following the report. The company denied the allegations, called the report inaccurate and misleading, and accused Scorpion Capital of trying to manipulate the market for financial gain.

By January 16, 2025, shareholder rights firms Bragar Eagel & Squire and Hagens Berman Sobol Shapiro were investigating whether TransMedics had misled investors or withheld important information. A regulatory petition also requested that the FDA suspend approval of TransMedics Organ Care System devices, particularly the OCS Liver device.

title: Red Cat promised a $55 million Army contract. Officials put the deal at $12.9 million.
points: It reviewed US Army budget documents showing a 2025 program budget of just under $25 million, and Customs and Border Patrol procurement plans of $1 million.
Short seller Fuzzy Panda Research published its own report while holding a short position.

Citing former employees and defense officials, it alleged that 60% of Red Cat's drones initially failed to work and that competitor Skydio had already delivered hundreds of drones for the same Army program.
body: Red Cat Holdings is a US drone manufacturer that told investors it had won a sole-source US Army short-range reconnaissance contract. Management projected $80 million to $120 million in revenue for fiscal year 2025, claiming its initial production deal would exceed $55 million.

On January 16, 2025, short seller Kerrisdale Capital published a report questioning those projections, noting it held a short position and profited if the shares fell. It reviewed US Army budget documents showing a 2025 program budget of just under $25 million, and Customs and Border Patrol procurement plans of $1 million.

On August 15, 2025, short seller Fuzzy Panda Research published its own report while holding a short position. Citing former employees and defense officials, it alleged that 60% of Red Cat's drones initially failed to work and that competitor Skydio had already delivered hundreds of drones for the same Army program.

On October 10, 2025, Fuzzy Panda Research published follow-up findings after contacting Army officials. The report said Army officials confirmed the Low-Rate Initial Production contract was worth only $12.9 million, and that Red Cat drones had been in the NATO catalogue since November 2023 without significant sales.

title: A data broker shared a sample file containing the location of over 47 million people
points: On January 15 and January 16, 2025, Le Monde and eight media partners published an investigation into the company.
The reporters examined a commercial presentation sample from Datastream Group's database that contained information on over 47 million people.
Le Monde published follow-up reports detailing the investigation into the database.
body: Datastream Group is an American data broker that sells and exchanges personal information for advertising purposes. The company now uses the name Datasys.

On January 15 and January 16, 2025, Le Monde and eight media partners published an investigation into the company. The reporters examined a commercial presentation sample from Datastream Group's database that contained information on over 47 million people.

Le Monde and its partners found localized data collected through mobile apps downloaded from the Google Play Store and the App Store, including Candy Crush, Vinted, Grindr, and Le Bon Coin. When contacted by the reporters, people identified in the file expressed surprise, and none of the confronted apps stated they had business relations with Datastream Group.
On February 12, 2025, Le Monde published follow-up reports detailing the investigation into the database.

title: FTAI sold whole engines and counted each one as three repair modules
points: Muddy Waters alleged that 70% to 80% of module sales were whole engines and that FTAI counted each whole engine sale as three separate modules.
Muddy Waters estimated that about 80% of Aerospace Products adjusted EBITDA came from gains on selling whole engines.
Muddy Waters presented the Iran sanctions allegations again in a series of slides on May 7, 2025.
body: FTAI Aviation Ltd. is a US aerospace company that leases aircraft engines and runs an Aerospace Products maintenance, repair and overhaul business. It told investors that its Aerospace Products revenue growth came from aftermarket module transactions, with an average transaction size of two modules.

On January 15, 2025, short seller Muddy Waters Research published a report based on public information and said it held a short position in FTAI securities. Muddy Waters alleged that 70% to 80% of module sales were whole engines and that FTAI counted each whole engine sale as three separate modules.

Muddy Waters estimated that about 80% of Aerospace Products adjusted EBITDA came from gains on selling whole engines. It also alleged that FTAI depreciated engines in its leasing segment before moving them into Aerospace Products inventory.

On March 3, 2025, Muddy Waters published a second report alleging that FTAI could have violated US sanctions on Iran. The investigator cited LinkedIn photos posted in January and February 2025 by an executive at Iranian repair shop Sorena Turbine showing two CFM-56 engines next to boxes with FTAI and Module Factory logos.
Muddy Waters presented the Iran sanctions allegations again in a series of slides on May 7, 2025.

title: SEALSQ raised $400 million at its spin-off, then lost 59% of its share price
points: BMF Reports published its own report examining SEALSQ's semiconductor business and crypto project.
BMF Reports noted that SEALSQ raised $400 million during its 2023 spin-off, but its shares fell from $14.73 in May 2023 to $5.99 on January 13, 2025, a 59% decline.
The $400 million was money raised at launch, while the 59% drop measured the fall in the share price.
body: SEALSQ Corp is a semiconductor company that spun off from WISeKey in 2023 and trades publicly under the ticker LAES. It told investors it had 1.6 billion semiconductors in the market, planned a global satellite network called WiseSAT, and launched a cryptocurrency called SEALCOIN.

On January 8, 2025, Martin Shkreli published a short report stating that SEALSQ had tried to ride the quantum computing wave. On January 13, 2025, BMF Reports published its own report examining SEALSQ's semiconductor business and crypto project.

BMF Reports alleged that the company rebranded off-the-shelf chips without manufacturing them and that SEALCOIN lacked technical details. It said the crypto project looked like a way to raise capital rather than a real technology breakthrough.

BMF Reports noted that SEALSQ raised $400 million during its 2023 spin-off, but its shares fell from $14.73 in May 2023 to $5.99 on January 13, 2025, a 59% decline. The $400 million was money raised at launch, while the 59% drop measured the fall in the share price.

title: Pentagon earmarks funded up to 86% of IonQ's revenue before they were canceled
points: Citing a former IonQ executive and academic lab data, the report alleged IonQ only had an 11-qubit machine in October 2020 and faced scaling delays.

body: IonQ is a US quantum computing company that told investors it had strong commercial demand and was delivering on technical milestones. In October 2020, executive Chapman claimed the company had a system with 32 perfect qubits.

On March 13, 2025, short seller Kerrisdale Capital published a report and said it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. Citing a former IonQ executive and academic lab data, the report alleged IonQ only had an 11-qubit machine in October 2020 and faced scaling delays.

On February 4, 2026, short seller Wolfpack Research published another report and said it was short the stock. Wolfpack alleged that Pentagon budget earmarks provided up to 86% of IonQ's revenue from 2022 to 2024 before being canceled in 2025, leaving a $54.6 million hole in anticipated quantum computing revenue.

Wolfpack also reported that eight IonQ insiders sold or authorized the sale of $396.6 million in stock under new trading plans after the Senate approved the fiscal 2025 budget. Those stock sales and the canceled $54.6 million in anticipated contract revenue are separate figures.

On February 4, 2026, IonQ denied Wolfpack's report as false, misleading, and unsubstantiated claims from a short seller trying to drive down its share price. The company said it was continuing to advance its position in quantum computing.

title: Two Fuji Media executives resigned, and a magazine took back part of its report
points: Tabloid magazines Josei Seven and Shukan Bunshun reported that a woman was invited to a dinner in 2023 where she was left alone with a celebrity TV host, Nakai, amid allegations of sexual misconduct.
Shukan Bunshun also reported that a Fuji TV executive had in a separate event gathered female TV personalities at a hotel as entertainment for Nakai and other celebrities.
Shukan Bunshun corrected its report and took back its claim that a Fuji TV executive had invited the woman to the dinner.
body: Fuji Media Holdings is a Japanese media company that operates a television unit.

Tabloid magazines Josei Seven and Shukan Bunshun reported that a woman was invited to a dinner in 2023 where she was left alone with a celebrity TV host, Nakai, amid allegations of sexual misconduct. Shukan Bunshun also reported that a Fuji TV executive had in a separate event gathered female TV personalities at a hotel as entertainment for Nakai and other celebrities.
A Fuji Media spokesperson said the company became aware of the woman's complaint that June, and did not widely investigate or report it due to privacy concerns and settlement talks.

On January 27, 2025, Fuji Media said Chairman Shuji Kanoh and TV unit head Koichi Minato would step down immediately, and promised an independent investigation by a third-party committee. Shukan Bunshun corrected its report and took back its claim that a Fuji TV executive had invited the woman to the dinner.
